Sports.title: Sex-mad former Barcelona wag stuns in blue and white bikini as fans label her ‘the most beautiful of all’
Sports.content:
A FORMER Barcelona Wag has wowed fans with a set of new bikini pictures.

Melissa Satta, 40, is the glamorous former bride of superstar forward Kevin Prince Boateng.



And though she is no longer with the 39-year-old ex-Ghana international, she has not lost an ounce of that stardom.

The Italian-American TV host and model continues to turn heads in the football world and beyond.



She is not shy about showing off her impressive physique to her adoring fans in a range of bold outfits.

And that was no different as she stripped down to a tiny bikini while soaking up the sun by the ocean.

She wore a blue bikini as she enjoyed the scenery in her native Sardinia.

Many of her 4.7million Instagram fans flocked to the comments to show their appreciation for the star.



One wrote: “Wonderful.”

While another said: “The most beautiful of all.”

Satta met Boateng in 2011 after he departed Tottenham Hotspur for AC Milan, and they quickly hit it off.



They were married in 2016, but split in late 2020.

Satta sensationally claimed that she was the source of some of his injuries due to their sex-filled private life.

And the same problem seemingly raised its head with her next partner, tennis star Matteo Berrettini.

Sports.title: Angry Atletico Madrid ultras plaster ‘Julian Alvarez OUT’ posters outside training ground as Arsenal get transfer boost
Sports.content:
JULIAN ALVAREZ has been targeted by furious Atletico Madrid ultras as uncertainty continues to swirl around his future.

Posters calling for the Argentina superstar to leave the club have been plastered outside Atletico’s training complex.



Pictures shared by Atletico Universe showed signs carrying the message “JULIAN FUERA” – meaning “JULIAN OUT” – around the entrance to the facility.

Another displayed Alvarez’s No19 shirt number inside a red prohibition symbol, with the protest reportedly organised by members of hardcore supporters’ group Frente Atletico.





Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

It marks an extraordinary deterioration in the relationship between the former Manchester City striker and sections of the Atletico fanbase following a summer dominated by talk of his departure.

And the unrest could provide another boost to Arsenal, who remain heavily linked with bringing the 26-year-old back to the Premier League.

Reports in Spain suggest Atletico would rather do business with the Gunners than allow Alvarez to strengthen LaLiga rivals Barcelona – the club believed to be the forward’s preferred destination.

Alvarez has made his desire to leave clear during a tense summer, although Atletico have repeatedly insisted they do not want to lose one of their biggest stars.



Diego Simeone has publicly backed the World Cup winner and described him as a key figure, but Alvarez was still left out of the squad for Wednesday’s 2-0 LaLiga-opening victory over Malaga.

Sports.title: Micky van de Ven and other overrated Dream Team players ahead of season opener
Sports.content:
THE wait is finally over!

Dream Team 2026/27 gets underway later today but there’s still time for managers to make use of their unlimited transfers to get their XI in shape for Gameweek 1.

PLAY DREAM TEAM NOW: £100,000 PRIZE POT!



Generally, we prefer to wax lyrical about strong options but it is also our duty to highlight players we believe to be overrated.



Such as…

Micky van de Ven (£3.5m)

The Tottenham centre-back is a smooth operator but why is he currently the fourth-most popular defender in Dream Team?

For starters, the Dutchman is a doubt for this weekend’s trip to Brentford, which should be enough cause to seek a replacement without further reasoning.

We’ve got reservations about his long-term viability too.

Van de Ven possesses immense recovery speed and he chipped in with six goals last season, only Virgil van Dijk (£5m) scored more among defenders.

But he simply hasn’t mustered all that many points in previous seasons, certainly not enough to warrant his current level of popularity.

Spurs have found clean sheets hard to come by in recent years and, without European commitments, Van de Ven’s schedule looks a tad light.



Furthermore, Jan Paul van Hecke (£3.5m) and Marcos Senesi (£3.5m) are both worthy of substantial minutes so it might be wise for Dream Team bosses to wait for a clear pecking order to emerge before committing to a Spurs centre-back.

Sandro Tonali (£3.5m)

It is not our intention to incite a Spurs pile-on but Tonali’s ownership of 10.6% looks excessive.

The Italian midfielder should improve the North Londoners as he seems well suited to Roberto De Zerbi’s philosophy but it doesn’t seem right that he’s more popular than the likes of Martin Odegaard (£4.5m), Florian Wirtz (£5m) and Ismaila Sarr (£4.5m).

Granted, those examples are from a higher price bracket but it’s curious that Tonali is comfortably the most selected £3.5m midfielder given the other options: Pascal Gross, Justin Kluivert, Iliman Ndiaye, Harry Wilson, Rio Ngumoha, Rayan, Emi Buendia… just to name a few.

Viktor Gyokeres (£5m)

We’ll caveat this by stating that the Arsenal striker would instantly become a solid option if selected to start against former club Coventry this evening.

However, Kai Havertz (£4.5m) was chosen to lead the line against Manchester City last weekend and justified Mikel Arteta’s decision with a goal — just as he did in the Champions League final.

At this moment in time, it seems like the German forward is above Gypokeres (12.5% ownership) in the pecking order.

Or perhaps the pair will have to share their minutes?

Either way, gaffers probably shouldn’t fork out £5m of their budget for a striker who isn’t a guaranteed starter.



Marc Guehi (£5m)

With an ownership of 7.4%, Manchester City’s No6 is just outside the ten most selected defenders.

Some would argue that number is scandalously low given Guehi ranked third among players in his position last season with 296 points to his name but we advise caution at the start of the new campaign.

The 26-year-old was late back from the World Cup and may begin the season as back-up to Ruben Dias (£4.5m) and Josko Gvardiol (£5m), who both started against Arsenal in Cardiff last weekend.

As with Spurs, the sensible play is to stay clear of Man City centre-backs until the pecking order has been established.



Injured Players

As an extension of this conversation, we can’t stress enough the importance of avoiding availability traps.

Far too many gaffers are about to start the season with injured players in their XI: William Saliba (£5m), Jurrien Timber (£5m), Eli Junior Kroupi (£4m), Brian Madjo (£2.5m), Kaoru Mitoma (£4m), Hugo Ekitike (£5m), etc.

And big names such as Bruno Guimaraes (£4m), Jeremy Doku (£5m) and Benjamin Sesko (£4m) are among those considered doubtful.

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba could be set for shock position change under Michael Carrick once £65m Man Utd transfer is completed
Sports.content:
CARLOS BALEBA could be handed a shock new role under Michael Carrick if he completes his £65million move to Manchester United.

The Brighton star is closing in on an Old Trafford switch as Carrick looks to put the finishing touches to his squad.



And while Baleba is being brought in to bolster United’s midfield, he could provide an unlikely answer elsewhere if Carrick is left short over, especially with European football this season.

The 22-year-old is left-footed and has previously played at left-back, as well as filling in at centre-back.



Dream Team is back, free, and there’s £100,000 up for grabs!

It does not seem like United are signing him exclusively to be a left-back but he could pitch in if needed.

In 2024, Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler noted that he was up for using Baleba as another left-back option for the Seagulls.



Hurzeler told The Athletic: “He is an option to play there.

“Against the ball he is very athletic. He has good speed, he is good one-against-one and with the ball.

“He can play very good vertical passes and he can create a dynamic from further back, because of his dynamic runs.”

Nevertheless, Baleba has only played twice at centre-back for Brighton and NEVER at left-back.



This dilemma comes after United flirted with a number of players this summer who can operate in both midfield and at left-back.

Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly was reportedly offered to the Red Devils by intermediaries earlier this month.

United were interested in the 19-year-old, who is comfortable in both positions, after he struggled for regular starts under Mikel Arteta last season.

But Lewis-Skelly is now expected to remain at his boyhood club and United have turned their full attention towards Baleba.

Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga, who has also filled in at left-back during his career, was another name on the shortlist.



United had explored a move for Baleba last summer but backed away after Brighton valued him at more than £100m.

They never completely took their eyes off the Cameroon international though and continued to track him throughout last season.

And talks with Brighton are now understood to centre on a deal worth around £65m.



Mason Mount’s fitness had initially left United debating whether another midfielder or a left-back should be next through the door.

The England international impressed in a deeper role during pre-season BEFORE lasting just 19 minutes against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Scans have revealed a minor hamstring injury – another concern after an injury-hit three years at Old Trafford.

Meanwhile, Luke Shaw – who started every Premier League game last season – turned 31 last month, making him the third oldest outfield United ace.

The Red Devils are still expected to sign a specialist left-back, although a move for Newcastle’s Lewis Hall has cooled off.

Sports.title: Mason Mount forced Man Utd into transfer U-turn after causing 'internal debate'
Sports.content:
Mason Mount forced Man Utd into transfer U-turn after causing 'internal debate'

Manchester United have already signed two midfielders this summer with Carlos Baleba set to become a third acquisition following an injury to Mason Mount in pre-season

View 2 Images Mason Mount is dealing with a hamstring injury ahead of the opening day of the season (Image: Getty Images)

Mason Mount’s latest injury setback forced Manchester United to pivot in the transfer market and pursue a new midfielder. The Red Devils entered the summer market in dire need of midfield recruits following Casemiro’s exit.

‌



And United bosses acted quickly with a £50m deal for ex-Chelsea man Andrey Santos, as well as a £35m move for Aston Villa’s Youri Tielemans. It appears that they are not quite done there though, with a deal reportedly close for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba.

‌



While the Cameroonian midfielder is a long term target - the club having also eyed him last summer - they might not have made a move for him had it not been for an injury to Mount. According to The Athletic, the former Chelsea man had impressed in pre-season and had convinced some behind-the-scenes that he could be the candidate to occupy the deeper midfield role.

‌



That decision had caused some at United to debate whether signing a new left-back should in fact be their top priority - with the likes of Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly linked, albeit that deal is now unlikely.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Mount, however, picked up a hamstring injury against Paris Saint-Germain, with scans revealing a minor issue. While that injury alone was not enough for United to completely change tact, it was a useful reminder of his injury issues, which triggered a renewal of the club’s attempts to sign a new midfielder.

‌



United initially attempted to look at players who could play both in midfield and at left back, hence the links to Lewis-Skelly, while Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga had been mentioned. But Baleba is now the man they are pursuing.

Asked about a deal, United boss Carrick said: "I just think we are looking to strengthen the squad. We are certainly working towards that, and making the most of the situation that we have and trying to improve things, trying to move forward.

"I said the same thing to you last time, so certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than when we went into it. I think we're in a good way to doing that."

‌



View 2 Images Man United are closing in on a deal for Carlos Baleba (Image: Getty Images)

The former midfielder also gave an update on Mount and his injury issues. He added: "Managing Mason [Mount] a little bit, but he is very close, so it is touch and go for the weekend really and going into next week.

"First of all, Mason is a top player. We have seen that so far. Pre-season, he was one of our best players in the early stages in the games that he played. I thought he was fantastic, not surprising what I have seen before, what I expect and what I know of him.

‌



"He has picked up a bit of a knock, there are no dramas. It is nothing major. Of course, he has missed some football over recent years, and he wants to be fit and wants to be in that full rhythm and wants stay fit, so we're doing our best to help him do that, but he is a top player, Mason.

"The same as recovery, we have got to manage the squad, there are going to be injuries through the season, and we have to have a squad that is strong enough to have a really good top starting team with depth to carry us through the season. Mason will be back very, very soon. If not immediately."

Sports.title: Four players could miss Arsenal vs Coventry as injury blows already confirmed
Sports.content:
Four players could miss Arsenal vs Coventry as injury blows already confirmed

Reigning champions Arsenal get their Premier League season underway tonight against Coventry City at the Emirates Stadium - but Mikel Arteta has a new fitness doubt

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta and Frank Lampard go head-to-head this evening as Arsenal host Coventry (Image: (David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Mikel Arteta is sweating on the fitness of Bruno Guimaraes heading into tonight’s game against Coventry City. Arsenal begin the defence of their Premier League title against Frank Lampard’s side at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Guimaraes, who joined the Gunners from Newcastle United earlier this month, was forced off during the Community Shield victory over Manchester City last weekend. And speaking on Thursday afternoon, Arteta admitted: "Let's see how it is, it's evolving well, but let's see for tomorrow."

‌



However, Arteta will be without defenders William Saliba and Jurrien Timber. Saliba is continuing his rehabilitation from a back injury sustained at the World Cup, while Timber remains sidelined with a long-term groin problem.

‌



“No, I said in the next few weeks,” Arteta said on Thursday when asked if Timber can join team training this week. “He's not training with the group yet.”

But there was better news for Gunners supporters, with Arteta confirming that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are fit to start against the Sky Blues. The Arsenal boss said: “Yes, they're ready to be involved, yes.”

Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas READ MORE :

While Frank Lampard confirmed on Thursday that Coventry will be without striker Haji Wright for the games against the Gunners. Wright was Coventry’s top scorer last season, scoring 17 times as his side won the Sky Bet Championship.

‌



The striker has been absent from recent friendly matches against RCD Espanyol and AS Monaco. And Lampard admitted his star man could be out for as long as 12 weeks. He said: “Haji Wright won’t be available for the Arsenal game.

“He won’t be available for a little while, he’s got a very serious quad injury which is disappointing for Haji and for us. It’s certainly going to be a number of weeks, could even be up to 12 weeks.”

Lampard, though, did confirm that both Ephron Mason-Clark and Jack Rudoni will be in contention to feature at the Emirates after they missed games in pre-season.

‌



View 2 Images Haji Wright won't be available for Coventry City (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The Coventry boss also admitted his side need to be ready for “tougher times” this season ahead of their Premier League curtain-raiser. He said: “We will go through tougher times this year for sure because of the competition we’re up against now so we’ll need resilience in moments calmness in moments.

‌



“An important part of my role is to have that balance and through having a long playing career through having a managerial career where I’ve had some really great moments and some difficult moments.

“But as a club we will need to stick together in those moments but I want to sound like I’m being too negative before something’s happened. It’s just a reality that we need to be ready for.

“Second spell at Chelsea wasn’t great for me, for a PR point. But having been through the challenges for good and for bad in my managerial career I think it puts me in a better spot to deal with – don’t get too high, don’t get too low – continue and focus on your.”

Sports.title: Tottenham set to sign Man City star Savinho as spending spree smashes £300m mark
Sports.content:
Tottenham set to sign Man City star Savinho as spending spree smashes £300m mark

Tottenham have spent heavily so far this summer following a dismal campaign and Roberto De Zerbi’s men are now set to raid Manchester City for two big-money signings

View 2 Images Spurs have agreed a deal to sign Savinho (Image: Getty Images)

Tottenham have agreed a deal worth up to £85m to sign Manchester City winger Savinho. The North London side are long-term admirers of the Brazilian winger, having failed to agree terms on a €50million (£43.3m) deal last summer.

‌



But they have retained their interest in the 22-year-old and are now close to finally securing his services. According to The Athletic, Spurs have agreed to pay £75m up-front for the former Troyes man, with £10m in potential bonuses.

‌



Should the deal go through as expected, it would represent a record sale for City, eclipsing the £81m sale of Julian Alvarez to Atletico Madrid in 2024.

‌



Savinho would also become the latest high-profile departure from the Etihad Stadium this summer, with Tijjani Reijnders, Rodri, James Trafford, Nathan Ake, Bernardo Silva and John Stones having all left alongside former boss Pep Guardiola.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The sales might not even be finished there, either. Spurs are also in talks with City over a deal for Egyptian forward Omar Marmoush.

‌



A deal for both him and Savinho is expected to cost around £140m - meaning Marmoush is valued at around £55m. The 27-year-old only joined City from Eintracht Frankfurt in January last year and has gone on to net 16 goals in 62 appearances.

Meanwhile, Savinho joined the club from French side Troyes in 2024 but has only netted twice in 53 Premier League outings.

Once their moves to North London are complete, they will become the latest arrivals in what has been an astonishing £369m rebuild under Roberto De Zerbi. Spurs have already signed Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke for big fees, while Marcos Senesi, Andrew Robertson and Martin Dubravka have all joined on free transfers.

‌



View 2 Images Omar Marmoush is expected to follow Savinho to North London (Image: Getty Images)

Spurs start their season against London rivals Brentford on Saturday evening, while Man City entertain Bournemouth on Sunday. Ahead of that game, City boss Enzo Maresca has already hinted that more signings could arrive before the deadline.

He said: "We knew already before the game the things that we need to do. It is not because we lost the game. We are quite clear. For sure, we are going to do something before the transfer window closes."

Article continues below

City have been linked with Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi but the Italian remained tight-lipped on a deal. He added: "He is still a Lille player. But any new signing as soon as they arrive, it’s better [for us], because we have the Premier League starting in one week."

Sports.title: Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas
Sports.content:
Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry City as Mikel Arteta faces selection dilemmas

Arsenal will kick off their Premier League title defence against newly-promoted Coventry City on Friday night and a few new signings could potentially be in line to appear for the Gunners

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is aiming to guide Arsenal to a second, consecutive title (Image: Getty Images)

For the first time in over 20 years, Arsenal head into a Premier League season as defending champions. The North London side waltzed to their fourth title under the stewardship of Mikel Arteta last term, finally getting over the line after years of near misses.

‌



And while the celebrations of them hoisting the trophy at Selhurst Park back in May will be fresh in the minds of every player and fan, it’s now back down to business.

‌



Arsenal kick off the defence of their title on Friday night as they welcome newly-promoted Coventry City to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Supporters have already managed to get a glimpse of the champions as they eased past Manchester City to win the Community Shield. New signings Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes were handed their debuts but did either of the pair do enough to start in Arsenal’s league opener?

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Before we answer that question, let’s start in defence where Gunners boss Mikel Arteta has a pretty simple task ahead of him. Last season’s Golden Glove winner David Raya will of course start between the sticks - and the defence in front of him effectively picks itself.

‌



Both William Saliba and Jurrien Timber are ruled out through injury, which opens the door to Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White. Brazilian centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes will partner the former in the heart of defence.

There’s then a debate to be had at the other fullback spot, where Riccardo Calafiori, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Piero Hincapie could all play. But given the Italian’s performance in the Community Shield, Arteta may just stick with what he already has.

Academy graduate Lewis-Skelly shone in Cardiff against City, so it feels very harsh to suggest that he could drop out. But Declan Rice is now fit and ready to go, Arteta did express some fitness doubts about new signing Bruno Guimaraes - but that's nothing new for the Gunners boss, he should still start.

‌



View 2 Images Declan Rice might start against Coventry (Image: Getty Images)

It’s also very difficult to envisage Arteta not starting captain Martin Odegaard for the Gunners’ Premier League opener.

When it comes to his attack, the Arsenal boss now has a wealth of options to choose from. Summer arrival Tzolis enjoyed a bright start to life with his new club in the Community Shield after notching two assists and that performance might well have been enough to earn a starting spot against Coventry.

‌



Noni Madueke started on the opposite flank against City, but Arteta might be tempted to draft in Bukayo Saka for a start.

There is then another debate to be had in the central attacking position, where Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyokeres and Gabriel Jesus are all options. The German scored against City - and appeared to have usurped Gyokeres in the pecking order at the end of last season - so is probably a good bet to start again.

Arsenal predicted XI vs Coventry: Raya; Calafiori, Gabriel, Mosquera, White; Rice, Guimaraes, Odegaard; Tzolis, Saka, Havertz.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 predictions as Arsenal tipped for title and £100m signings flop
Sports.content:
Finally, the wait is over. The 2026/27 Premier League season is finally here.

The new campaign gets underway on Friday evening as defending champions Arsenal take on newly-promoted Coventry City. The two sides have very different ambitions for the upcoming campaign, but for this weekend at least, they are equals.

And that goes for each of the 18 other top-flight clubs, who have made managerial changes, dipped into the transfer market and have gone through gruelling pre-season campaigns.

All of that work will now be given its toughest examination yet as the real stuff gets underway. But what's going to happen throughout the next 10 months?

‌



Mirror Football writers have taken a look into their crystal balls to find out...

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Daniel Orme

Winners: Arsenal

The Gunners are the complete package under Mikel Arteta. They've got a brilliant attack, a formidable midfield and a solid defence. And they've now got the silveware to prove it. With the vast majority of their rivals now in transition, the path is opening up for Arsenal to claim the title yet again.

‌



Top five: Arsenal, Man Utd, Liverpool, Man City, Chelsea

Michael Carrick will be hopeful of carrying on the momentum that United built up last season into the new campaign and seal a Champions League spot. Liverpool and Manchester City also have good enough squads to finish in the top four. Chelsea should also be good enough but a title challenge looks like a pipe dream.

Relegated: Coventry City, Hull City, Fulham

It's easy to tip the promoted clubs to go straight back down and I fear two of them will be slipping back into the Championship in 10 months' time. Hull City have a squad that's simply not good enough for the demands of top-flight football, while Coventry will make more of a fight of it but will still be relegated.

‌



Ipswich's experience of a couple of years ago should see them improve. That could leave a surprise package nervously looking over their shoulders and I think that could be Fulham, who could take some time to adapt to Alvaro Arbeloa's demands so could be playing catch-up.

Surprise package: Leeds United

Daniel Farke's side have upgraded in all of the positions that they needed to this summer - and with some of their established rivals contending with European football, that could see the Yorkshire side take advantage. It would certainly not be a shock to see them secure a spot in the Europa League next season.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

‌



Do I need to explain this one? He's the best striker in the Premier League. He's the best striker in the world. And he will be claiming the golden boot once more.

View 7 Images Haaland looks set to win another golden boot (Image: Getty Images)

Best signing: Youri Tielemans

Given the extortianate market when it comes to central midfielders this summer, Youri Tielemans for just £35m is a bona fide bargain. He adds some serious quality to the heart of the United midfield. And under Carrick, he should be able to elevate his game to even higher levels. It would not be a surprise to see the Belgian seal a number of wins with his penchant for an eye-catching goal.

‌



Biggest flop: Mateus Fernandes

This feels slightly harsh given he's just 21 years of age. But is Mateus Fernandes an £85m midfielder? I'm not totally convinced that he is.

Could he be? Possibly. But as it stands...not quite. That price-tag means that he'll be expected to have an instant impact but I think his contributions will be limited this season which could see the pressure rise.

First manager sacked: Alvaro Arbeloa

‌



Having tipped the Londoners for relegation, I'm also predicting Arbeloa to be cut adrift. He's got no Premier League managerial experience and very little full stop. If and when the chips are down at Craven Cottage, I don't expect Fulham to wait for him to pick them back up.

James Whaling

Winners: Arsenal

With Manchester City in transition and none of the other clubs yet ready to challenge the Gunners, I can see this being something of a procession. After finally ending their long wait for a title, I fully expect Mikel Arteta to go back-to-back and lift the trophy again in May.

The arrival of Bruno Guimaraes makes their already formidable midfield stronger and Christos Tzolis looks an exciting attacking addition.

‌



Top five: Arsenal, Man City, Man Utd, Liverpool, Chelsea

I still expect City to be Arsenal's nearest challengers, mainly due to the firepower of Erling Haaland. Manchester United should carry on their upwards momentum under Michael Carrick and it will be fascinating to see how a reintegrated Marcus Rashford performs. Liverpool should have enough to complete the top four under Andoni Iraola and I fancy Xabi Alonso to return Chelsea to the top table of European football.

Relegated: Coventry, Hull, Crystal Palace

It's always tricky for the promoted sides, unless you're Regis Le Bris' Sunderland, and this year looks like being no different. Hull did incredible to return to the top flight but it's hard to see them beating the drop. Similarly Coventry, back after 25 years and with a feel-good factor under Frank Lampard, but look up against it. Crystal Palace might be a surprise pick, but their manager is a complete unknown and some of their business has been headscratching.

‌



Surprise package: Ipswich

I'm backing the Tractor Boys to break the mould and stay in the Premier League. I think they will benefit from their brief foray in the top division two years ago, albeit under a different manager in Gary O'Neil, who will also reap the benefits of his experiences with Wolves and Bournemouth. Julio Enciso and Abdul Fatawu look like smart additions at the top end of the pitch.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Do you really want an explanation?

‌



Best signing: Christos Tzolis

OK, so the Belgian Pro League isn't the Premier League. But 43 goals in all competitions from the wing in the last two seasons speak for themselves. Tzolis looks like an upgrade on Leandro Trossard and made a bright start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield.

View 7 Images Christos Tzolis has already had a bright start to life at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Biggest flop: Elliot Anderson

‌



I want to quantify this, because 'flop' is probably too harsh. I don't think Elliot Anderson is a bad player, or a bad signing. But the transfer fee makes me uncomfortable. He is not a £116million footballer, and that is no slight on his ability. He is also not in the same calibre as Rodri, the player he is tasked with replacing. He's a perfectly good player and well worth his place in the England side. But I cannot seeing him having the impact his price tag should justify.

First manager sacked: Sergej Jakirovic

Hull face Manchester United, Aston Villa and Chelsea in their first four games, travelling to fellow new boys Coventry in the other. A slow start looks very possible and pressure could be on the Tigers boss from early in the campaign.

‌



Sam Meade

Winners: Arsenal

The Gunners finally got over the line last season and that ended the one nagging doubt you had about them. They've strengthened their squad this summer and their closest challengers are all embarking on new eras, which will make overhauling the champions a tall order.

Top five: Arsenal, Man City, Chelsea, Liverpool, Man Utd

Man City by no means inspired in the Community Shield but have too much to not be up there again whilst Xabi Alonso is perhaps the most impressive of the new managers at top clubs, which could help the Blues make huge leaps. Michael Carrick will see that playing in four competitions makes things a lot harder at Manchester United.

‌



Relegated: Coventry, Ipswich, Hull

This year we could see a return to the unfortunate scenes that has seen all three promoted sides going straight back down. Frank Lampard's Coventry will give survival the best shot, but still fall short.

Surprise package: Newcastle

Despite all the doom and gloom, understandably, I still think they'll be in Europa League contention, which isn't bad for a team who've lost the bulk of their best players, their manager and finished in the bottom half last season.

‌



Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Not much to say here, he's utterly elite. A fourth Golden Boot in five seasons would have him among the Premier League's greatest strikers, not that he isn't already.

Best signing: James Trafford

Had some standout moments for Man City as they won the Carabao Cup last year and, now in a Leeds team that will look to further consolidate themselves in the top flight, the goalkeeper will really start making his case to be the Three Lions No 1 in the not too distant future.

‌



Biggest flop: Alejandro Garnacho

His last two years have almost been write offs in Manchester and then Chelsea, Aston Villa now think they can get a tune out of him but Garnacho hasn't look like fulfilling his potential for years. The Argentine has moved on loan, which could become permanent, but this is a risky move, and one that won't pay off.

View 7 Images Alejandro Garnacho is now onto his third club in as many seasons (Image: Getty Images)

First manager sacked: Sergej Jakirovic

‌



The Hull owner is an ambitious man and after gaining promotion despite finishing in sixth, he'll know his window for making the Tigers a Premier League team could be a small one. If he can tempt a good manager to Yorkshire, he will do so as early as possible.

Felix Keith

Winners: Arsenal

What don’t they say about north London buses? You wait 22 years and then two come along at once.

Even before signing Ezri Konsa and the world-class forward we’ve been promised all summer, Arsenal have the best squad and their closest rivals are undergoing rebuilds. It’s a recipe for success.

‌



Top five: Arsenal, Man Utd, Man City, Liverpool, Brighton

Enzo Maresca and Andoni Iraola are going to encounter all sorts of problems as they rebuild this season, leaving the door open for Manchester United to pip them to the best of the rest. There’s something to be said for stability and in Michael Carrick they have that. The failure to shift Marcus Rashford could end up being a blessing in disguise.

Like most summers, Chelsea appear to be a mess, with Xabi Alonso wading through unwanted players every time he arrives at Cobham. Tottenham will improve after splashing the cash but not enough to make it into the top five, leaving Brighton to build on their momentum.

Relegated: Fulham, Hull, Ipswich

‌



Ipswich have spent over £100million on players this summer, but the departure of Kieran McKenna after promotion is a blow they won’t bounce back from. Hull look well short of Premier League quality. And I really fear for Fulham in the post-Marco Silva era. The Portuguese manager made mid-table mediocrity look easy, but Alvaro Arbeloa won’t, sending them down just above a succession of disappointments, in the form of Nottingham Forest, Newcastle and Everton.

Surprise package: Brighton

The Seagulls have finished eighth in the last two campaigns and I fancy them to improve upon it this time around. Much like Bournemouth, their recruitment tends to be spot-on and I could see them building up a head of steam in Spring 2027, despite losing top scorer Danny Welbeck.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

‌



It’s obvious for a reason. He’s won the Golden Boot in three of the last four Premier League seasons and the fact Brentford’s Igor Thiago was the closest to him last time around says a lot.

Best signing: Jeremy Jacquet

Losing a player for nothing is never ideal, but swapping Ibrahima Konate for Jacquet could prove to be a timely upgrade. The Liverpool centre-back pairing of Konate and Virgil van Dijk was ropey last season and Jacquet brings class and composure at such a young age to Liverpool’s backline.

View 7 Images Jeremy Jacquet is set to replace Ibrahima Konate at Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Biggest flop: Sandro Tonali

I am simply not having £100m for Tonali, who Newcastle fans will tell you was really not that good last season. The Italian is a good midfielder, nothing much more, and Tottenham have grossly overpaid for his services.

First manager sacked: Oliver Glasner

Quiz question: can you name the four managers Nottingham Forest cycled through last season? No cheating. Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis is not a patient man and I’m not sure Glasner is convinced he’s made the right choice after leaving Crystal Palace. If things go south early in the season, the Austrian could be toast.

‌



Andy Dunn

Winners: Arsenal

And while you’re at it, give them the 27-28 title as well. It has been clear for some time that this is an Arsenal squad - and manager - capable of establishing an era of domestic dominance.

A great goalkeeper, a formidable defence and a powerhouse midfield give Mikel Arteta the basis for a team that should rarely be beaten. Add a bit more high-end creativity and firepower, and they could even be invincible.

Top five: Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool, Chelsea, Manchester City

‌



United’s transfer business has not been overly dramatic but has been shrewd enough to add to the momentum built by Michael Carrick last season. Andoni Iraola will take a while to become accustomed to the demands of Anfield but will get motoring after a couple of months and Xabi Alonso will restore some sensible football to Stamford Bridge. The post-Pep void will be more painful than City fans imagine and they will only just scrape into the top five.

Relegated: Coventry City, Hull City, Ipswich Town

Deeply unimaginative, for sure, and let’s hope it’s not the case. But it is hard to make a really compelling argument for any of the promoted teams avoiding a relegation battle. One or two of them might battle their way to a points tally that keeps them up but it’s hard to be confident about that scenario. If you are looking for outsiders to get sucked in, Everton and Nottingham Forest might be on your list.

Surprise package: Leeds United

‌



He has been in the firing line a few times but Daniel Farke makes a nice contribution to the Premier League product and his team will continue to entertain. And with James Trafford on board, they have a reliable last line of defence. They will defy their odds.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Even though it will be a season of struggle for Manchester City, Haaland will do what he always does and dominate their scoring charts. It would not be surprising if Alexander Isak gives Haaland a run for his money and if you are looking for a long shot, look no further than Manchester United’s Benjamin Sesko.

Best signing: Morgan Rogers

‌



At £117million, the England man is not the best-value signing but he will flourish under Xabi Alonso at Chelsea and flourish alongside Cole Palmer.

James Trafford is a corker of a capture for Leeds United.

View 7 Images Morgan Rogers completed a big-money switch to Chelsea earlier this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Biggest flop: Sandro Tonali

‌



For this era of over-priced midfielders, the Italian is probably the poster player. At £116million, Elliot Anderson will come under scrutiny at Manchester City but Tonali’s price tag - £92.5million rising to £100million - is preposterous. He is not going to single-handedly transform Tottenham Hotspur’s fortunes, that is for sure.

First manager sacked: Sergej Jakirovic

Again, hardly left-field, but the Hull City manager faces a formidable challenge to put points on the board and will be vulnerable early in the season.

Alex Richards

Winners: Arsenal

‌



Hard to back against Mikel Arteta's men. They've consistently improved in the last two years, won the title last term to finally get that monkey off their back and were penalty kicks away from being European champions. Could they be more expansive and exciting? Of course. But they overpower opponents, grind teams down and look like making fewer mistakes than any of their rivals.

Top five: Manchester City, Manchester United, Liverpool, Chelsea

If it looks like the obvious answers, it's because they are. Aston Villa have lost too many key players, Chelsea don't have Europe to contend with and have a new workaholic manager with a point to prove, while City, United and Liverpool all look shoo-ins. Tottenham will improve but probably have too much room to make up.

Relegated: Hull City, Coventry City, Fulham

‌



Of the three promoted teams, I think Ipswich, can keep their heads above water. They've really strengthened and while Kieran McKenna may have gone, Gary O'Neil comes in looking to show that the manager we saw in his final half season at Wolves - ironically sacked after losing at home to the Tractor Boys - isn't really who he is. In his first season at Wolves, and his year at Bournemouth, he did very well to ensure both survived, and can do so again at Portman Road.

If they're staying up, then someone from last season's top-flight mix has to go down, and Fulham are the team who I'm very uncertain about. Along with the exit of Marco Silva, some key, experienced performers have been allowed to depart for pretty minimal sums and they've spent very heavily on the young Real Madrid pair Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, both known to new boss Alvaro Arbeloa. They don't have an easy start to the season and I think they could be running into a big problem.

View 7 Images Alvaro Arbeloa could struggle in his first season as Fulham boss (Image: Getty Images)

Surprise package: Everton

‌



After finishing 13th last season, I think David Moyes will have them in contention for European places this term. Hayden Hackney is a talented player who should dovetail nicely with Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, Tyrique George is talented and will want to show Chelsea they were wrong. Moyes teams tend to trend upwards in their second full seasons and if they can find a regular goalscorer, be it one currently in situ or a new arrival, then they'll be much improved.

Top goalscorer: Erling Haaland

Next.

Best signing: Andy Robertson

‌



It's been a while since Spurs had anything like a settled defence and they've had issues at left-back for quite some time. Robertson may be 32, but for what Roberto De Zerbi is going to want, he's absolutely ideal, especially considering his arrival as a free transfer. His determination and leadership qualities should also help drag up standards that have too often in the last few years been allowed to slip.

Of all the others, Joao Gomes should help Aston Villa fill a big hole in their midfield while Ousmane Diomande will shine in Oliver Glasner's back three at Nottingham Forest.

Biggest flop: Gonzalo Garcia

Fulham need him to be red hot from the off and throughout the season after paying £34m up front for the young Spaniard, but I'm just not sure he's going to be able to give them what they need as he adapts to not only a new country, but what is effectively his first full season as a bona-fide starter in senior football.

‌



First manager sacked: Sergej Jakirovic

He may have got Hull City promoted, but that won't count for much if they're struggling come the international break.

Sports.title: Arsenal complete £51m Konsa deal
Sports.content:
Arsenal have completed the £51m deal to sign defender Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.

The England international has signed a four-year contract with the option of an additional 12 months after passing his medical, with only official confirmation of the deal remaining.

The 28-year-old could now make his Arsenal debut against his old club at Villa Park in the Monday Night Football on August 31, live on Sky Sports.

Aston Villa

Arsenal Monday 31st August 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

Konsa has become Arsenal's fifth major summer signing after Piero Hincapie joined permanently from Bayer Leverkusen and the arrivals of Illan Meslier, Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes.

Konsa's arrival comes after the Premier League champions were looking for a new defender with William Saliba out for an extended period of time, while Jurrien Timber remains sidelined with a long-term groin problem.

Villa had initially held out for £60m, with Arsenal hoping to pay much less, but the two clubs found a compromise on Thursday to strike a deal for the former Brentford defender.

Arsenal also looked into a potential move for Bayer Leverkusen's Jarell Quansah but have chosen to sign his England team-mate Konsa. Both players have a similar profile and can play at right-back and centre-back.

Image: Arsenal have completed a deal for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa

Analysis: Konsa is a perfect Arteta player - here's why

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

If there's one thing you need to know about Mikel Arteta, it's that he loves players that win duels. Nobody was better at it than Ezri Konsa last season.

He won more duels on the ground than any other Premier League player last season - finishing quite some distance ahead of his nearest challengers Virgil van Dijk and Gabriel - his new team-mate.

With both Saliba and Timber out injured, Arsenal were in need of a player who can cover both right-back and centre-back roles.

The Gunners do have Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White as cover in those roles - and both performed well in the Community Shield win over Manchester City - but the latter has a lengthy injury record over the last two seasons.

Arsenal also saw the importance of having good depth at right-back when Mosquera was forced to start the Champions League final with PSG out of position - with the young Spaniard conceding a penalty.

Now a move for Konsa has been completed, Arsenal have filled an important part of their team - and would be very close to completing their transfer window from an incomings point of view.

Can they find the forward player they have been looking for?

Sports.title: Billam-Smith expects Opetaia showdown in 2027
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith expects to fight Jai Opetaia next year, if they are both victorious in their upcoming bouts.

Former world champion Billam-Smith has long targeted Australia's Opetaia, widely regarded as the best cruiserweight in the sport.

Opetaia will box Noel Mikaelian on the undercard of Conor Benn's fight with Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas on September 12.

Billam-Smith should fight again before the end of the year and then intends to resume his pursuit of Opetaia.

It's a showdown he believes will happen in 2027.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Rozicki was pulled out of the fight after the seventh round following an instant classic with Chris Billam-Smith.

"I think so. I think I need to get through my next fight and then I'll fight the winner of that, whoever that might be," Billam-Smith told Sky Sports.

"Mikaelian on his day is a good fighter but I pick Jai to beat him.

"But it might take him a few rounds to set the pace and obviously Mikaelian's got some good names on his record, has some good performances but I feel like he's slowed down a little bit and gone a little bit past it now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports Boxing commentary team watches on in disbelief as Ryan Rozicki takes some huge shots from opponent Chris Billam-Smith in their Zuffa Boxing 07 main event.

For his return to action Billam-Smith said: "Looking most probably around November time.

"I think it will be London or Bournemouth. Don't know who yet.

"The champions seem a bit tied up, I think [David] Benavidez is lining up a fight for December as well in Vegas, I believe."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chev Clarke bounced back from being put down twice in the fourth round as he went on to stop Jack Massey in the seventh round of their cruiserweight classic.

Cheavon Clarke caught the eye with a knockout, comeback victory over Jack Massey on the undercard of Billam-Smith's barnstorming battle with Ryan Rozicki.

"Obviously Chev won on my undercard. He's got two [amateur] wins over me so from a competitor's point of view I'd very much like to get one back," Billam-Smith noted, speaking to Sky Sports at a screening of new boxing drama Fightland.

"[Clarke-Massey was] a superb fight which I think was definitely going to win fight of the night - until our fight."

Both Clarke and Massey were amateur foes of Billam-Smith's, and both of them beat the Bournemouth man in elite championship finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chev Clarke recovered from being knocked down twice to stop Jack Massey in the seventh round of their enthralling clash.

He wants revenge. "I owe him one and I feel like that does the Jack Massey one in the ABA final as well. Both of those have beaten me in an ABA final. That would put that to bed so that would be nice," Billam-Smith said.

"I'm up for whoever," he added. "Zuffa are signing people all the time so you just don't know who's going to pop up out the woodwork and get offered. So we will see on that front."

Billam-Smith lost his WBO championship to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and beat Brandon Glanton in his only bout of last year. But June's thunderous collision with Rozicki showed that the 36-year-old can still perform in top-level contests.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chris Billam-Smith found out just how tough Ryan Rozicki was after the Canadian took nine clean shots from The Gentleman.

"I think if I'd taken my foot off the gas and was just sort of coasting I would definitely have been beat that night. I think that's the important thing to take away from my point of view," Billam-Smith said.

"I had to be switched on and pushing the training as I do and looking for different ways to improve.

"I'm on it. And I'm still getting better."

Fightland is coming to Sky and NOW on August 27.

Sports.title: Rise of Espanyol's English winger Dolan: 'I am not the player I was a year ago'
Sports.content:
Tyrhys Dolan made an explosive start to the season in LaLiga with a goal in Espanyol’s 3-0 win over Levante. The English forward looked particularly sharp. Something has changed. “I am not the person or player I was a year ago,” Dolan tells Sky Sports.

His first year in Spanish football after leaving Championship club Blackburn Rovers had its moments. He played against Real Madrid and Barcelona. But there is more to come, he insists. "I know the league now. I know myself a lot more. I know what I can do."

There is a reason for his optimism. Dolan spent much of last season operating on the right wing. "Pretty much on the touchline. Hanging wide." His job was to cross the ball and his numbers reflected that. "My assist output was much better than my goal output."

It was a learning experience that added to his repertoire. But now Dolan is back on the left. That role change brings new opportunities. "For me, it is better because I can cut in and get more shots off. I can be more dangerous as a left winger," he explains.

"Which way is he going to go?" he asks, imagining the dilemma facing the defender. "Is he going to take it and put across? Is he going to have a shot?" The change has already brought a goal. And it can bring more. "There are more avenues to my game."

Speaking to Dolan, 24, his enthusiasm for the challenge ahead is infectious. Last season turned into a slog for Espanyol after a strong start. They went from chasing Europe in the winter to the very real prospect of relegation in the spring. The slide was alarming.

"You'd be lying if you sit there and say you don't feel the energy around the stadium. We just don't want to have a repeat of that." That big win over Levante suggests something has changed. The buzz is back. "It was just like, yeah, now we're off and running again."

Image: Dolan celebrates his goals with a somersault

The summer has refreshed him. It was a chance to spend time with family and friends, important for a young man living alone in Barcelona. "Mentally, you need that switch off. Within the season, you are constantly preparing, dealing with emotions, good or bad."

He adds, poetically: "Absence, like they say, does make the heart grow fonder." It is why Espanyol spending much of pre-season in England was a boost. "My mum and dad were at every single game." But, encouragingly, part of him also missed his life in Barcelona.

"It was nice, that feeling, knowing that they were only an hour or so up the road," he says. "But for me, being in Barcelona means being in work mode and as an athlete you love it in that environment. You start missing it when you are away from it for too long."

Image: Dolan believes he is a different player to a year ago

Dolan has already shown in that game against Levante that he is ready to go again. "It was the perfect way to start. It is that reward for the hard work put in, a confidence boost for the team and obviously for myself too." But there are bigger tests ahead.

Espanyol host Real Madrid on Saturday evening in what will be the first game of the season in LaLiga for the 36-time champions of Spain. Jose Mourinho is back in charge. Kylian Mbappe, in Dolan's view, the best player he faced last season, will be there too.

He called that first meeting with Madrid a pinch-me moment. Now, it feels a little different. Still exciting, but he is approaching it with "a cooler head" and is unconcerned whether his opponent at right-back will be Trent Alexander-Arnold or Denzil Dumfries.

"Anybody. These are the games that you want to compete against the best so that you can bring your best and see where you are at." And his best is changing. "I was happy with what I did in my first season. But I know it is nowhere near what I know that I can do."

The challenge now is to show what he can do on the biggest stages and perhaps bring out that trademark somersault celebration against the world's most famous football club on Saturday. "I felt like I could give more for this team, for the club, for the supporters."

A chance to show that Tyrhys Dolan is a different player now.

Sports.title: Spurs agree £85m deal to sign Savinho from Man City
Sports.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have agreed an £85m deal with Manchester City to sign Savinho.

Spurs will pay an initial £75m for the Brazil international, with a further £10m available in add-ons.

It is understood that £5m of the potential bonuses are effectively guaranteed, meaning City could receive at least £80m from the deal.

The 22-year-old is scheduled to have a medical with Tottenham on Friday afternoon.

Spurs also remain in talks with Man City over a separate deal for striker Omar Marmoush as they look to further strengthen their attacking options.

Brentford

Tottenham Hotspur Saturday 22nd August 5:00pm Kick off 5:30pm

Savinho, who has played a bit-part role since joining Manchester City in 2024, started only seven of his 24 Premier League appearances last season, in which he scored once and set up two goals.

Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six first-team players this summer. They spent £185m on two midfielders, Sandro Tonali and Matheus Fernandes, from Newcastle and West Ham respectively.

Jan Paul van Hecke joined from Brighton for £52m to replace Cristian Romero.

Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson and Martin Dubravka all arrived on free transfers.

How are Spurs spending so much money?

At the start of the transfer window, Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge explained how Spurs are able to spend big this summer...

"We're told there are absolutely no concerns about falling foul of the Premier League's financial rules.

"The club is in great financial health after qualifying for Europe in 18 of the last 20 seasons. The revenue driven by the stadium is huge: boxing, concerts, NFL games - you name it.

"In fact, in the Deloitte Money League, the rankings show that Tottenham Hotspur have leapfrogged Chelsea to become the ninth richest club in the world with annual revenues of £549.2m.

"On top of that, Spurs are one of the clubs to benefit most from the Premier League's shift to squad cost ratio from PSR, which has just come into effect. But the reason we're seeing Spurs spend so much is a shift in strategy under new leadership.

"Daniel Levy left at the start of last season, and there's a real desire to spend the money to dine at the very top table.

"Now the new leadership and the owners promised fans, after avoiding relegation on the final day, that they would spend the club's revenue on the first team, and they are delivering on that."

'City will want to replace Savinho and Marmoush'

Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom:

"Both players [Savinho and Marmoush] are essentially surplus to requirements at Manchester City. It's been pretty apparent through the summer. Enzo Maresca has said that in the case of both players, they are very much entitled to stay and fight for their first-team place.

Manchester City

"But equally he understands, a bit like James Trafford, when a player wants to play first-team football and they're not guaranteed the starting shirt, then the club, if they receive an offer that's acceptable, will not stand in their way. That applies to both players.

"City would need to replace these players. They would definitely, I'd say, have to replace one. They would like to and would aim to replace two.

"But the transfer window is closing in less than a fortnight. These are big positions to fill so late in the window."

Sports.title: Hadjar hopeful of Italian GP return after wrist injury
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar is hopeful he can return for the next Formula 1 race after a wrist injury forced him to miss this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix.

Hadjar suffered the injury while boxing in training during the summer break earlier this month and will be replaced by Liam Lawson, who becomes the first driver to race again for Red Bull having previously being dropped by the team.

Yuki Tsunoda will take over Lawson's seat at Racing Bulls alongside full-time driver Arvid Lindblad.

Sky Sports News understands Hadjar suffered a small crack in a bone in his wrist late last week in a routine workout before discussions with Red Bull medical staff led to the decision to miss the Sprint weekend at Zandvoort to allow more time for recovery before the next race at Monza.

Hadjar is at the track this weekend at Zandvoort to support Lawson and is hopeful of a return at the Italian Grand Prix, which takes place on September 4-6.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hadjar tells Karun Chandhok he's pleased with how he's performed alongside Max Verstappen at Red Bull

Lawson: I'm much more comfortable compared to 18 months ago

Lawson was dropped from Red Bull after two disappointing races last year but did enough over the remainder of the 2025 season at Racing Bulls to retain his seat for this year.

The 24-year-old has been one of the stars in the midfield this season with eight points finishes and sits ninth in the Drivers' Championship - only behind the Mercedes, McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull drivers.

"I've had a lot more races since then [being dropped from Red Bull]. I feel much more comfortable racing in this sport, but it's going to be a very challenging weekend, for sure," said Lawson.

"It's a Sprint weekend, so it's going to be a quick learning process. But that's what we're focused on, that's what we tried to do in the simulator. If we can try and speed up that learning process as much as possible, then that would help our weekend."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lawson sits down with Sky Sports F1's Crofty to reveal his the tracks he'd take with him to a desert island

Tsunoda has been watching from the sidelines this year and has an opportunity to impress to find a seat on the grid in 2027, albeit his options appear to be limited following the recent re-signings of Verstappen at Red Bull plus Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon at Williams.

The Japanese driver revealed he was on holiday in Greece before getting a call on Tuesday to get ready to drive for Racing Bulls.

"When I heard, I was like half excited, half still doubtful because anything can happen, but I was super excited too," he said.

"It was all confirmed that I'm racing this weekend. I'm super excited and physically I'm feeling ready. I've done a couple of TPCs [Testing of Previous Cars]. It will be my first time in this car but still, I'm very excited.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yuki Tsunoda admits he feels excited, but 'half doubtful' about the pressure of stepping up into the RB seat for the Dutch Grand Prix

"As far as I understand, I will be in the seat for now - this weekend - and also it depends on Isack's recovery. I hope that recovery goes pretty fast. I'm not sure about the next Grand Prix but my objective is to have fun. I've been waiting for a long time. I was watching the screen for the last few months.

"Since the season started, I've been dying to be in the car and compete with the drivers. This moment I will just enjoy, and obviously give my 100 per cent performance. Hopefully that will bring some good results."

Sports.title: Sixtygeesbaby and Safari Dream lock horns at Ffos Las
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Friday with flat action from Ffos Las, live on Sky Sports Racing...

2.10 Ffos Las - Recent winners Sixtygeesbaby and Safari Dream headline

The opening Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap is a belter where Sixtygeesbaby and Safari Dream headline six runners.

Sixtygeesbaby had been showing signs of a revival on his last few starts before claiming a Carlisle handicap earlier this month and a similar effort would put him in the mix.

Safari Dream looks an obvious threat for Rod Millman and Finley Marsh. Rated much higher in the past, he bounced back to winning form over this course and distance and makes plenty of appeal despite a two-pound rise.

Pull The Rug could be the pick of the remainder.

3.20 Ffos Las - Korbut, Likeness and Reader seek elusive first victory

A trappy affair with just the three runners for this Ascona Ladies In Lace Maiden Stakes at 3.20pm.

Korbut has claimed silver on five of her seven starts including the last four runs this summer. Rated 73, she should make a bold bid if able to reproduce her latest run back on the turf.

Marcus Tregoning saddles Reader who has a little to find of official figures but is lightly raced and may have more to give over this extra distance.

Likeness will be popular as he makes his debut for Jack Channon having left the George Boughey team. Top-rated on 74, she will need to be monitored in the betting on this return from 138 days off.

Kaleidoscope Eyes and Oviedo face off in the Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap at 2.45pm.

Oviedo was third in an Acomb back in 2022 and he now contests much shallower waters for the Alexandra Dunn yard. He showed he still retains plenty of ability when winning by a staggering 12 lengths at this track last week and he is well-in under this five-pound penalty.
