Tottenham have secured a £75m deal plus £10m add-ons for Manchester City star Savinho

Daily Mail Sport first reported Spurs' rekindled interest in the winger in late May of this year

Savinho, 22, will have a medical before signing a long-term contract. The Brazilian's move has been over 12 months in the making, with Spurs first attempting to sign him last summer.

After finishing a second-consecutive season 17th in the Premier League, Tottenham have recruited bullishly this summer in a bid to stop the rot.

Spurs have spent £185m on bolstering their midfield with the eye-catching signings of Sandro Tonali from Newcastle, and West Ham's Matheus Fernandes, with the club's business not yet finished.

Sports.title: 'Banned because refs can't do their job': Championship star is handed two-match ban for 'successful deception' with handball goal in incredible decision which has left fans of ALL clubs furious
Sports.content:
West Bromwich Albion star Aune Heggebo has received a two-match ban after scoring a goal with his arm – but the retrospective decision has incensed supporters online.

Heggebo netted the effort during the Baggies' 2-1 win against Norwich at Carrow Road on Saturday, when he bundled in a cross from new signing Jimmy-Jay Morgan after the ball struck his left arm.

Norwich players surrounded referee Tim Robinson – who had missed the incident – to protest the handball, but the goal stood with no further intervention from the officials.

Days later, however, and West Brom were unable to overturn the FA charge that Heggebo had 'successfully deceived a Match Official by handling the ball in a direct successful attempt to score a goal'.

The 25-year-old is now set to serve a two-match suspension for the offence, which is believed to be the first of its kind in English football since a 2024-25 rule change.

But fans on social media suggested that the punishment did not quite fit the 'crime', claiming instead that officials were at greater fault than the Norwegian striker.

Aune Heggebø’s goal for West Bromwich Albion against Norwich City has fuelled controversy over an alleged handball.



Should the goal have stood? 💭 pic.twitter.com/TcKQ4ctV9N — ITV Football (@itvfootball) August 15, 2026

Fans have hit out at the decision to penalise Aune Heggebo for his handball goal on Saturday

'Not sure about that at all,' one fan wrote. 'It’s the officials’ fault for not spotting it.

'The lack of VAR comes with clangers like this, which will always be a major talking point but that’s a very dangerous precedent to be setting.'

Another added: 'This is an absolute disgrace. A ban because the officials can't do their job. Wow.'

A third agreed: '2 game ban because refs are pony. Blows my mind how much protection they get ( feels good being able to say this now ).'

'A player has been banned because the officials failed to spot a handball for a goal,' another supporter commented. 'Joke.'

West Brom had first appealed the charge on Wednesday, with their statement published after the charge was upheld explaining that their claim had been that 'the ball took a deflection from the goalkeeper immediately before making contact with Heggebo’s arm, which materially affected the ball's trajectory and left him with less than 0.1 of a second to react.

'Given the accidental nature of the handball, the club argued it could not be reasonably viewed as a deliberate act of deception,' the statement added.

West Brom also threw their continued support behind their player, going on to add: 'We remain steadfast in our support of Aune, whose character and integrity have been evident throughout his time at The Hawthorns.'

At full-time after the match, Norwich manager Philippe Clement also reserved blame for the officials.

'It was clearly with the arm that the player scores – we could see that from where we were watching, 50 yards away,' Clement said after the game. 'It was the decisive moment in the game and should have been spotted.

'There are four officials and one of them should have seen it. Maybe the referee didn't have the best view – but the linesman on our side needs to see that.

'Missing game-changing moments like this shouldn't happen – it has cost us at least two, maybe three points.'

Sports.title: Arsenal complete Ezri Konsa signing: Premier League champions land Aston Villa star in £55m move hours before beginning title defence
Sports.content:
Arsenal have completed the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. England defender Konsa, 28, has signed a four-year contract with an option for a further year with the Premier League champions. The 28-year-old had his medical on Thursday ahead of completing his £55m move from Aston Villa - the fee is £51m plus £4m in add-ons. The Gunners' latest signing arrives hours before they begin their title defence against newly-promoted Coventry City at the Emirates Stadium. The fee is a triumph for Villa as Arsenal initially valued the 28-year-old, who had two years remaining on his contract, at £30m. He was not part of Unai Emery's squad for the UEFA Super Cup defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week as he was away on holiday after the World Cup. Arsenal have signed Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa in a £51million deal

Your browser does not support iframes.

Konsa featured 48 times last term in all competitions, scoring two goals and contributing one assist, as Unai Emery's side lifted the Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League to secure Champions League football for 2026-27. He also sported the armband in John McGinn's absence as Villa's vice captain. Konsa played in every game of England's World Cup run as the country finished third. Konsa started seven of the Three Lions' eight matches at the tournament, with Thomas Tuchel largely partnering him with Marc Guehi at the heart of the defence. He also filled in at right back during England's quarter-final victory over Norway.

Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE PREDICTIONS: Our experts pick which side will win title, who will go down, biggest flop and best new signing ahead of the new season
Sports.content:
It's been a long 12 weeks since the final day of the 2025-26 season but football fans can finally rejoice - the Premier League is back.

With a bang, too. Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea, and Newcastle are just a clutch of the boldfaced names with new managers to keep an eye on, and anticipation is rising to see the summer rebuilds clubs have ushered in.

Now, on the eve of the return of top-flight football, Daily Mail Sport experts Oliver Holt, Ian Herbert, Mike Keegan, Kieran Gill, Lewis Steele, Matt Barlow, Bobby Manzi, and Riath Al-Samarrai make their final predictions.

Tip to win the Premier League

Oliver Holt: Arsenal – they have made two good signings over the summer so far and sold prudently. They have strengthened from a position of strength. They look like a side that will be liberated by the confidence of being champions.

Ian Herbert: Arsenal - crossing the Rubicon to claim the title means so much, removes so much pressure. An excellent transfer window has made them stronger

Arsenal have got the devil off their back by wining their first Premier League title under Mikel Arteta and look stronger than ever

Chelsea welcome Xabi Alonso to Stamford Bridge unburdened by European football and having made key summer signings

Mike Keegan: Chelsea. We saw last season what an absence of European football can do at Manchester United and I like what I have seen at Stamford Bridge this summer given their recruitment pivot. The manager is top class and the old heads they have brought in could be enough for a stunning title assault.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Arsenal. They have the best squad, the least turbulence and have dismantled the mental barriers that previously dominated these conversations. The team to beat.

Kieran Gill: Arsenal. They are more settled than everyone else with Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea going through transitions under new managers. I’m not sure it will even be a close title race.

Lewis Steele: Arsenal. Best team by a distance last season. Manchester City were only close because the Gunners kept on stumbling and keeping them alive. Now, Mikel Arteta’s men will not have the tag of ‘bottlers’ or ‘chokers’ and that will free them up. I’d not be surprised if they won by 10 or more points.

Matt Barlow: Arsenal. Long time since they won back-to-back but strong and stable with main rivals in various degrees of flux. Bruno Guimaraes will improve them. Confident in the knowledge they have what it takes. Free from the anxiety of old.

Bobby Manzi: Arsenal appear stronger than last season, so this will no doubt be proved foolish come the end of the season. But Chelsea have an intelligent manager, have added experience to their squad and no European football to contend with - enabling them to focus on domestic glory. Alonso, against all odds, won the league invincible at Bayer Leverkusen. Chelsea look a good outside bet.

Completing the top four

Oliver Holt: Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea. For different reasons, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak had disappointing seasons with Liverpool last season. Both can flourish this year and Liverpool have new signings to complement them. Chelsea have a first class manager, no European commitments and a more realistic recruitment policy. City have the muscle-memory of previous greatness.

Ian Herbert: Chelsea, Tottenham, Manchester United. Something about Roberto de Zerbi’s energy allied to the big spending makes me think Spurs will be a big story this season. Chelsea on the up, too, but transition time for Manchester City and Liverpool

Mike Keegan: Arsenal will not be far off. You can’t judge City on a Community Shield but, for me, the jury remains firmly out on Enzo Maresca. Liverpool will improve under Andoni Iraola.

Alexander Isak endured a difficult first season at Liverpool but will be a major weapon fully fit

Riath Al-Samarrai: Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea. I don’t envision any of them making a sustained run on Arsenal, but a lot will depend on how quickly Liverpool adapt to Iraola’s style. That’s typically a slow process and a rapid finish. I can see them leading the chase.

Kieran Gill: Chelsea in second, City in third, Liverpool in fourth. Perhaps I’m thinking a tad optimistically on behalf of Xabi Alonso, but he is a good manager who has wielded his influence this summer.

Lewis Steele: Liverpool. People are sleeping on the ability of a much-improved Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Their XI is very good but beyond that, it is a worry. Manchester City because they have a deep squad and did not deserve the overreaction or ridicule that came after losing a glorified friendly but losing Pep Guardiola, Bernardo Silva, Rodri and John Stones in the same summer rips their heart out. I’ll go with Chelsea in fourth as I like Xabi Alonso.

Matt Barlow: Chelsea, Liverpool, and Man City. I'm expecting Xabi Alonso to get a tune out of the mass of talent at Chelsea, Liverpool’s big signings from 2025 to improve and City to fade post-Pep Guardiola and post-Rodri but still have lots of quality and Erling Haaland’s goals.

Bobby Manzi: Arsenal, Man United, Man City. Arsenal are nailed on for the top two but will find the first couple of weeks without William Saliba difficult. Manchester United have executed intelligent summer business - they had to improve their midfield and they have. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba are a great blend. As long as Michael Carrick was not a one-hit wonder, they will be up there. A new era at Manchester City but they still have a strong squad to creep into the top four.

The three going down

Oliver Holt: Newcastle almost got sucked into a relegation battle last season. Since then, they’ve lost their biggest asset, Eddie Howe, and their three best players, Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali. Their Saudi owners appear to have disconnected. I like Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich boss, but Ipswich are a classic yo-yo club. And I don’t think Hull have enough to stay up.

Ian Herbert: Fulham, Coventry and Ipswich. Fulham seem a perfect storm: inexperienced new manager, good players have left, an attempt to introduce new system to a club lacking intensity last season. There’s a bond about Hull City. I suspect they’ll be OK.

Newcastle have seen their ranks depleted and a successful manager depart ahead of the start of the season

Mike Keegan: Sunderland, Ipswich Town, Hull City. I’ll probably be the only one predicting Sunderland and I wish I wasn’t because they’re a great club with great fans but they massively overachieved last season and European football this time around could be a killer.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Hull, Ipswich, Fulham. That’s putting a certain amount of faith in Coventry, but Fulham have lost a strong manager and their best player in Harry Wilson. I think they’ll struggle.

Kieran Gill: Ipswich, Hull, Sunderland. I have a hunch that Coventry under Frank Lampard will surprise us, while Sunderland may struggle juggling European football with everything else.

Lewis Steele: Going to be boring and say the three promoted teams. I do think Sunderland will struggle from a bit of second-season syndrome but I think they have just enough quality with Enzo Le Fee, Granit Xhaka, Brian Brobbey et al.

Matt Barlow: Ipswich, Hull, Coventry. Those coming up can all take inspiration from last season’s survivors and there some established teams should be worried by the radical summer of change including Newcastle, Fulham and Palace but the gap still yawns.

Bobby Manzi: Coventry, Hull, Ipswich. Quite simply, the promoted sides are not better than any of the other 17 sides. Coventry have the best chance of staying up but they are lacking in defence.

The biggest overachievers will be

Oliver Holt: Spurs – they have bought well in the summer and in Roberto de Zerbi, they have one of the best managers of this generation. Like Chelsea, they have no European football to drain their resources. They’ll put their recent struggles behind them in style although they could do with a new striker.

Ian Herbert: Everton - drab end to last season obscured the way that David Moyes, such a fine and still underrated manager, has rescued them from annual purgatory. Some good recruits this summer. Moyes buys well. Europe calls.

Mike Keegan: Chelsea, followed by Coventry, who I think will defy the odds and stay up.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Brentford. Again. A smart club with a smart plan and they haven’t been raided quite like Brighton, who would be my second choice if they didn’t have to content with European commitments.

Kieran Gill: I may have hinted at this in my previous answer, but I’ll plump for Coventry. I’m not saying they will suddenly secure Europe. That’s a stretch. Somewhere towards the midtable would be cool.

Lewis Steele: A Brighton or Bournemouth could really flourish but may be held back by Europe. After finishing 17th twice in a row, lowly relegation fodder Spurs might climb up the table…

Tottenham have recruited intensely over the summer, luring Sandro Tonali from Newcastle in a bid to avoid a third 17th-place finish in three seasons

Matt Barlow: Leeds - finished last season at a gallop and reinforced in the summer market. Three winnable home fixtures to start at fortress Elland Road can build a platform for a strong season as others from mid table tackle complications of Europe

Bobby Manzi: Brentford. They were so close to Europe last season - missing out on goal difference. Many tipped them to go down under Keith Andrews and they defied expectation. This season, they may just get Europe. With Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Brighton all playing on Thursday nights, the teams in the middle of the pack could suffer a drop-off in the league. Brentford have kept the majority of their squad from last season together and added sprinkles of quality such as Mamadou Sangare in midfield. They appear well positioned.

The biggest underachievers will be…

Oliver Holt: Manchester City – I know I’ve got City down to finish in my top four but I don’t think they’ll challenge for the title. It’s always tough when a great manager leaves a club after a long time in charge and I don’t think it will be any different for City. It’s a huge test for Enzo Maresca.

Ian Herbert: Newcastle – car crash summer from a club the Saudis couldn’t be bothered to administer properly, now led by a managerial novice. You’re well out of it, Eddie.

Mike Keegan: Manchester United. There is time left in the transfer window for United to strengthen but, as things stand, I do not think they have made the additions which will deliver another Champions League finish.

Riath Al-Samarrai: A three-way tie between Manchester United (thin squad), Newcastle (decimated squad and technical area) and Aston Villa (great expectations after last season but a pretty horrible summer of departures).

Kieran Gill: Aston Villa. As good of a manager as Unai Emery is, Villa have sold some big names this summer, from Morgan Rogers to Lucas Digne to Youri Tielemens, so I’m concerned they may struggle.

Aston Villa have seen their squad stripped of a number of key talents and have European tests to come later in the season

Lewis Steele: Newcastle. The bubble has burst. I did think it was probably right for Eddie Howe to move on but losing Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon in the same window stinks.

Matt Barlow: Aston Villa. Challenging season ahead for Unai Emery. Lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne. Ezri Konsa leaving. Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins unsettled. Key staff gone, too. And has a Champions League campaign to plot.

Bobby Manzi: Bourmemouth. It’s only natural to have a comedown after last season, finishing sixth on 57 points and securing Europa League football for the first time. Much like with Palace last season, playing Thursday-Sunday will take its toll domestically. A bottom-half finish but a strong European return for the Cherries.

Player of the season

Oliver Holt: There are early signs that Arsenal may have cast off the nerves that afflicted them last season. If they play with more freedom and justify their tag as favourites, Bukayo Saka may rediscover his best form.

Ian Herbert: Declan Rice was the orchestrator and architect of so much about Arsenal last season. I can see him running a side that’s feeling mentally released and free.

Mike Keegan: Cole Palmer. A summer off is incredibly rare in this world of saturated football and the mysteriously-omitted England winger will have a barnstormer.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Easy answer would be Haaland, again, but I’ll go with Odegaard at Arsenal. He looks fit and sharp again, which wasn’t always the case last season, but it’ll be interesting to see how Arteta constructs the puzzle with Rice and Guimaraes (who might well be the star turn – the guy can do everything).

Cole Palmer has had a summer off after an injury-stricken season and should be raring to go

Kieran Gill: Joao Pedro. Just because of what I’ve seen of him in Chelsea’s handful of pre-season games. He’s looking like a superstar, and it is understood he is set to sign a new contract.

Lewis Steele: Since I cover Liverpool I will keep my regular readers happy by going with Isak. I’ll look silly when he does his hamstring on Sunday.

Matt Barlow: Alexander Isak. Back to full fitness after his awful first season at Liverpool and sure to enjoy Andoni Iraola’s full throttle style.

Bobby Manzi: Erling Haaland. Goals, goals, goals. At the World Cup, Haaland proved he can find the back of the net regardless of who is around him - scoring seven in five matches. He’s a machine. Nobody will get close to him.

Signing of the summer (so far)

Oliver Holt: Jordan Henderson – not just because he still retains much of the quality he had in his prime but because he is a symbol of a change in approach that Chelsea desperately needed. Xabi Alonso has some brilliant young players at his disposal but it has to be leavened with experience and Henderson and Danny Welbeck are fine professionals who will provide that.

Ian Herbert: Bruno Guimaraes will look even classier in a world class midfield and his presence will free up Rice. Some tandem they’ll be. The £75m salary may come to look excellent value.

Mike Keegan: Youri Tielemans. For the first time in a long time, Manchester United have signed a player who looks like a Manchester United player. I think he’ll settle quickly at Old Trafford and a much-needed all-round presence in midfield.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Harry Wilson to Leeds for nothing.

Kieran Gill: Arsenal’s £75m landing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle. He should fit into that midfield beside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard nicely.

Bruno Guimaraes represents a coup for Arsenal's recruitment after his move from Newcastle

Lewis Steele: I like some of the low-key ones like Joao Gomes to Aston Villa and Ousmane Diomande to Nottingham Forest and Antonio Silva to Bournemouth. But for the sake of picking one I’ll go Matheus Fernandes.

Matt Barlow: Maxence Lacroix. Should bring much needed leadership and maturity to the heart of Chelsea’s young team and not bad value in today’s world of head-spinning fees.

Bobby Manzi: Youri Tielemans. Manchester United have been gradually improving their squad to mount a title charge by 2028. Last season they bought a new forward line; this season it is the midfield. £35million for one of the best midfielders in the league who is in his peak is the best pound-for-pound signing of a window where midfielders are moving for £100m-plus. Technical Tielemans will give United control of games from deep alongside contributing goals and assists.

The signing I'm not sure about is…

Oliver Holt: It hasn’t happened yet but if it does, I think Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City would be a mistake that would upset the balance and the ethos of the club.

Ian Herbert: Andrey Santos. A curious and very substantial £50m layout on a player who doesn’t really seem to have proved himself as a stellar talent at Chelsea. Odd summer for United.

Mike Keegan: James Trafford. I like Trafford. He’s down-to-earth, a character and clearly a talented shot-stopper. However, in this era of set-piece coaches and goals from corners, I do wonder if he has the physical presence to ensure he lives up to his £40m fee.

Riath Al-Samarrai: Sandro Tonali at Tottenham. The price tag is astronomical.

Kieran Gill: Alejandro Garnacho. Aston Villa have taken a chance on him with a loan – and a conditional obligation to buy – and he has a ton to prove.

Alejandro Garnacho remains a risky deal for Aston Villa after his uneven season in west London

Lewis Steele: Carlos Baleba to Manchester United if it happens. Brighton fans don’t seem bothered about him leaving.

Matt Barlow: Elliot Anderson. Quality player but a huge fee brings great expectation and a difficult time to join Manchester City at the end of an era.

Bobby Manzi: Luka Vuskovic. A teenage defender with a very high ceiling but £50m is a significant outlay for a centre-back who hasn’t played in the Premier League and still has plenty of development ahead of him. He will make mistakes this season - he’s young. Brighton just have to hope he fulfils his potential and eventually reaches his projected future sell-on value. After all, their model is based on calculated risks.

Manager with the most to prove

Oliver Holt: It has to be Enzo Maresca. Following Pep Guardiola is the toughest task in world football and that is Maresca’s fate. Far from universally popular at Leicester City, he left Chelsea in difficult circumstances. I’m not sure he has the personality or the people skills to lead a club of City’s size. If he does, he will join the elite of world coaching.

Ian Herbert: Enzo Maresca. The expectation will be that the prophet of Pep will simply pick up his reins, but history, his own temperament and the Community Shield tell us otherwise. Spectre of those 115 Premier League charges still a shadow on the wall.

Mike Keegan: Xabi Alonso. He got the big gig and, to say it didn’t go well, would appear to be a significant understatement. Arrives at Stamford Bridge with a big point to prove post-Real Madrid, and I think he will do just that.

Enzo Maresca is stepping into enormous shoes at the Etihad as he replaces his former boss Pep Guardiola at Man City

Riath Al-Samarrai: Enzo Maresca at Manchester City, obviously. Seemed a little too pleased with some half-decent work at Chelsea and those shoes he is filling at City are huge.

Kieran Gill: Enzo Maresca. Following Pep Guardiola is no easy task, but Manchester City paid Chelsea a total of £17m to hire him. That brings immediate pressure at a club used to winning.

Lewis Steele: Enzo Maresca. Everyone is out to get him as we saw with the vultures descending on a glorified friendly defeat against the best team in the country. He has a lot of doubters to silence. Same goes for Andoni Iraola, Xabi Alonso, the list goes on…

Matt Barlow: Enzo Maresca. Just the 15 major trophies in 10 years for Pep Guardiola, follow that.

Bobby Manzi: Alvaro Arbeloa. Arbeloa is a bit of an unknown quantity. Interim at Real Madrid for five months at the end of last season, having previously held youth roles, this is his first genuine crack at senior management. His record at Real was okay with a 64.29 per cent win rate, losing eight games. That would be more than acceptable at Fulham, not so much at Real. But he was credited for how he lifted the dressing room after a tough spell under Alonso. Fulham have enjoyed stability in recent years under Marco Silva: Arbeloa must show he can provide that.

Sports.title: Man United boss Michael Carrick says it is 'ridiculous' to suggest they have an easy start against Hull and Ipswich - and plays down talk of a Premier League title challenge
Sports.content:
Man United boss Michael Carrick says it is 'ridiculous' to suggest they have an easy start against Hull and Ipswich - and plays down talk of a Premier League title challenge

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Carrick says it’s ‘ridiculous’ to suggest Manchester United have been handed an easy start to the season – and admits it’s asking a lot for his team to be considered title challengers.

United kick off the campaign at Hull City on Saturday lunchtime followed by a first home game against another of the newly-promoted teams, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford the following week.

But Carrick has rejected claims that United have been given an easy ride, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous.

‘It’s a tough start against both teams, but we’re not getting past Saturday. A newly-promoted team away from home will be a tough game.

‘That is the beauty of the new season. For teams coming up into the league, there tend to be quite a few changes. That is the challenge playing against them, we are fully aware of that. Mentally and physically we have done a lot of work. We are fully aware of what’s at stake and what’s coming at us.’

On United’s chances of delivering a first Premier League title since 2013 while coping with the demands of a Champions League return, Carrick added: ‘It’s going to be a jump. It doesn’t matter whether I say whether we can or can’t – and I would never say we can’t – it’s about what we can do, and what we are capable of doing as a group.

Carrick has rejected claims that United have been handed an easy start to the season, saying: ‘There are no favourable starts. It’s an easy thing to throw out there but pretty ridiculous'

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba (right)

‘The run of form we had last season gives us confidence, but we know there is a whole new step to make as a group. We have the potential to achieve things and we have to believe we can do good things.’

United hope to add a third midfield signing of the summer after tabling a £65million offer for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, having already spent £85m on Andrey Santos, of Chelsea, and Aston Villa’s Youri Tielemans. The club are also keen to strengthen at left-back.

Carrick was reluctant to say too much with another 11 days to go until the transfer window closes. ‘I just think we are looking to strengthen the squad, and we are working towards that,’ he said. ‘We’re certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it, and I think we are in a good way to doing that so far.’

Marcus Rashford’s return from a loan spell at Barcelona has given United another option, and Carrick has been delighted with the England international’s attitude so far.

‘It has been pretty obvious that Marcus came back training with Kobbie (Mainoo) and Licha (Martinez) that he has come back fantastically well,’ added the United boss. ‘He looks strong, sharp and ready to play football. He can play through the middle, even though it’s not his No 1 position. We have forwards that give us that flexibility.’

Carrick had some positive injury news with Mason Mount close to fitness after missing the final two friendlies against Leeds and AC Milan with a foot injury. Benjamin Sesko, Matthijs De Ligt and new No 2 goalkeeper Karl Darlow, none of whom featured in pre-season, are also back in training.

‘Karl has trained this week, he is in good shape,’ said Carrick. ‘Mattha has been out for a long period of time, but he is training, and it’s great to have him back. He won’t be involved but he is in good shape and moving in a good direction, so that is a bonus for us. Ben is back training so that is another positive and we’re looking forward to having him back around the group and getting him some minutes.

‘We’re managing Mason a little bit, but he is very close. He’s touch and go for the weekend really and going into next week. Mason will be back very, very soon, if not immediately, so it's all good.’

Sports.title: Olly Murphy throws open his stable doors to public during National Racehorse Week
Sports.content:
Olly Murphy throws open his stable doors to public during National Racehorse Week

The top jumps trainer is aiming to cater for up to 2,000 people who will get a behind the scenes glimpse of the operation of a major racing stable

View 3 Images Olly Murphy: expecting 2,000 visitors (Image: PA)

Top jumps trainer Olly Murphy is throwing open his doors to up to 2,000 members of the public next week determined to show horse racing in the best possible light.

‌



Murphy will be joined by champion jump jockey Sean Bowen at his 145-box yard at Wilmcote, near Stratford-Upon-Avon, at the event on Tuesday, one of the biggest stable visits to be staged during National Racehorse Week.

‌



Over ten days from August 22 to 31, 96 different racing venues across England, Scotland and Wales will be open to the public, alongside over 50 community events and three city activations held at some of England’s biggest cities and landmarks.

‌



Race meeting abandoned after two jockeys sent to hospital following heavy falls READ MORE :

Amazing Journey to be aimed at £5 million race in Australia after purchase for major stable READ MORE :

And the sport is coming to the heart of London for the first time when the public can meet a racehorse, at one of four city pop-up racing yards. Two will be held in Liverpool and another in Portsmouth.

Spaces are available for more than 15,500 people to attend public events this year, an increase on last year's figure of 14,800 free spaces available to book. During the event there will be 111 public open days across 96 venues including: 76 training yards, 11 studs and nine aftercare centres

Murphy has been a staunch supporter of National Racehorse Week, believing he has a duty to show the sport’s commitment to horse welfare.

‌



View 3 Images Sam Quek and Chris Hughes in Chester during National Racehorse Week (Image: PA)

“We are opening our gates to an unlimited number,” he said. “We are at a very important stage in horse racing and this gives the wider public an opportunity to see what we do.

“I am very keen to have the public come in and see how these horses are looked after, spend the morning with us and meet myself and the staff and see how we operate.”

‌



As well as Bowen signing brochures, Murphy will put on various demonstrations of the operation of a racing yard.

View 3 Images Chris Hughes went behind the scenes at Jackdaws Castle to launch the UK’s first National Racehorse Week (Image: PA)

“This is not about me trying to get new business or new owners, it’s just to welcome everyone into Warren Chase who might not have seen a racing yard before or even those who have.” he said.

Article continues below

“It’s important we can show off our sport and what goes on behind closed doors. Anyone who hasn’t got the greatest perspective of how a racehorse is looked after and is very inquisitive please come along and see the love, care and attention we give these horses.”

National Racehorse Week runs from the 22nd to 31st August 2026. Bookings open on 15th July.

Sports.title: Coleen Rooney beams with joy as she reveals Man Utd starlet son Kai's GCSE results
Sports.content:
Coleen Rooney beams with joy as she reveals Man Utd starlet son Kai's GCSE results

Coleen Rooney has shared her reaction after her Manchester United prospect son Kai received his GCSE exam results

View 2 Images Coleen Rooney shared her reaction to Kai's GCSE results (Image: Instagram/@coleen_rooney)

Coleen Rooney has announced that her son Kai has passed all of his GCSEs. The 16-year-old Manchester United youngster marked results day alongside his mother, who shared a photo of them grinning together.

‌



Kai, son of club legend Wayne, has been part of United's academy since returning to the club at the age of 11 and recently signed a first-year scholarship deal. The agreement enables Kai to continue his studies while going through United's academy system. He could potentially sign a professional contract once he turns 17.

‌



The teenager's footballing progress was disrupted last season after picking up a season-ending injury in March, sidelining him for the FA Youth Cup final against Manchester City. He had enjoyed a breakthrough campaign before the setback, making his debut for Darren Fletcher's under-18s at the age of 15 and scoring twice while providing an assist across six U18 Premier League outings.

‌



Kai also made his first appearance at Old Trafford last season, featuring for 21 minutes in United's FA Youth Cup fourth-round triumph over Derby County. Having watched her eldest son balance his footballing dreams with his school work, Coleen was delighted to share Kai's exam results on social media.

‌



In an Instagram post, Coleen wrote: "GCSE results day!! Super proud @kairooney.10... Great results, especially with a busy schedule, all passed and a place in 6th form!! We love you."

It represents yet another landmark moment for Kai, who is striving to strike a balance between his education and desire to emulate his dad. Wayne did not sit his GCSEs at Kai's age, but pursued self-education later in his playing days.

The former England star previously told BBC Sport: "It's no secret that I didn't even take GCSEs but I think people assume because of that that I'm not educated, which is really wrong. I made a conscious effort when I was at Everton and Manchester United to educate myself in a lot of different things, such as black history and religion.

‌



"The reason I did that was because I wanted to hold conversations with my team-mates who are from different backgrounds. That was something I did to help me with my team-mates and help understand how they have been brought up. That's probably something people don't understand about me."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Meanwhile, Kai returned to the pitch last week after recovering from injury and was part of United's squad for the Otten Cup in Eindhoven. The midfielder confirmed his comeback on Instagram with the caption: "First game back from injury. PSV (A)."

‌



United suffered a 1-0 defeat to hosts PSV in their opening fixture of the tournament, with Kai also part of a 23-man squad that featured Jacey Carrick, son of United boss Michael Carrick. Kai's comeback arrives at a crucial point in his development, as he could become a key player for the U18s this season.

The teenager previously banned his dad from attending games because of the attention Wayne would receive on the sidelines. The 40-year-old was in the stands to watch Kai make his Old Trafford debut last season but later admitted he was underdressed for the occasion.

Sports.title: Endrick responds to Liverpool offer as Reds plot Jose Mourinho transfer revenge
Sports.content:
Endrick responds to Liverpool offer as Reds plot Jose Mourinho transfer revenge

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has plenty of previous with Liverpool from his time managing Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur over the years

View 2 Images Endrick is said to be enjoying Real Madrid training and seemingly wants to stay this summer (Image: Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Endrick is reportedly not considering leaving Real Madrid despite Liverpool apparently being interested in the Brazil international. The Reds are said to have inquired about his availability after they signed Yan Diomande.

‌



Liverpool were willing to spend almost £100million on the Ivory Coast international, who ultimately chose Madrid over Merseyside. Diomande has since detailed the involvement his new coach, Jose Mourinho, had on signing him, telling SportyTV : "Mourinho got up at five in the morning to talk to me."

‌



He recalled: "When Madrid calls you, you can't say no. So I said: 'If they want me, that's where I'll be'."

‌



Liverpool receive Brighton response after launching £50m Yankuba Minteh transfer bid READ MORE :

Despite the 19-year-old's signing increasing competition going forwards, ESPN claims that Endrick wants to stay after enjoying training this summer. Mourinho is said to believe the forward can be a versatile attacking option.

Both the coach and player have apparently rejected offers from Aston Villa and Roma over recent weeks. After spending the second half of last season on loan at Lyon, Endrick has featured for Mourinho during pre-season this month.

The 20-year-old started and scored in his first outing of the summer against Fiorentina. Endrick also started their friendlies with Deportivo La Coruna and Ferencvaros, but did not feature last time out.

‌



View 2 Images Jose Mourinho reportedly values Endrick as a versatile attacking option for Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Diomande made his non-competitive debut in Endrick's absence, replacing Brahim Diaz for the final half-hour. The former RB Leipzig winger has spoken highly of Mourinho since arriving in the Spanish capital.

In the same interview with SportyTV, he said: "As soon as I arrived, he told me: 'I promised you that you were going to be part of my team, and here you are.' And I told him: 'I'm happy to work with you because you are the best.'

‌



"I can learn a lot from him; he is the right coach to continue my development. I am prepared to die for him."

The latter has since joined the former at Paris Saint-Germain, with whom Liverpool have been in talks for several weeks regarding Bradley Barcola. PSG want £140million for the France international, who has made clear privately that he wants to sign for the Reds.

Sports.title: Liverpool made to give up Premier League privilege as Arsenal reap rewards
Sports.content:
Liverpool made to give up Premier League privilege as Arsenal reap rewards

There will be notable difference to Arsenal's kit this season

View 2 Images Liverpool's loss has been Arsenal's gain (Image: PA)

Liverpool have been forced to give up a perk after relinquishing the Premier League title to Arsenal. The Gunners will begin a season as defending champions for the first time in 22 years when they host Coventry City on Friday, while Liverpool visit Newcastle on Sunday.

‌



Aside from introducing new kits, there will be a notable difference in the shirts of both sides compared to last season. The gold Premier League badge, which is added to the sleeve of the champions' shirt, has been removed from Liverpool's and handed to Arsenal.

‌



The gold badge was first added to the champions' kit for the 2015/16 season, meaning the Reds have had the honour twice, while the Gunners will enjoy the privilege for the first time. That privilege extends to the fans, who have been adding the patch to their own replica shirts in their droves since May.

‌



Following an impressive 3-0 victory over Manchester City in the Community Shield on Sunday, Mikel Arteta's side look well placed to retain the title and the coveted gold badge.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arteta said the result and performance showed the Gunners are ready for the defence of their crown. He said: "The desire comes [because] I want to live that moment again.

‌



Arsenal chief makes transfer window vow as Mikel Arteta shortlist revealed READ MORE :

"I want to live other moments, even bigger than them. We know what it's going to take. We know the difficulty of the task.

"We've never done it at this club, to win it again. We know that it’s going to demand something special and we are ready for it."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The Gunners are favourites to successfully defend their title, especially after putting down such an impressive marker against opponents expected to be their closest rivals.

Arteta added: "We talked about the desire we have to start the season and to show ourselves how much we want it, I saw a lot of positive things against a top opponent.

View 2 Images The gold badge that adorned Liverpool's shirt last season (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

"I am obviously extremely happy with the performance, the result, and winning the first trophy. I think it is down to the preparation we have done in pre-season.

"To the decisions the boys took after the World Cup, to continue to get prepared, to come early because they wanted to be part of it. If we drive the standards at this level, I’m sure that we’re going to be really, really competitive."

Sports.title: 11 pundits predict who will win Premier League title with BBC stars in major disagreement
Sports.content:
11 pundits predict who will win Premier League title with BBC stars in major disagreement

With the start of the new Premier League season almost upon us, we're looking at who the nation's top pundits are tipping to lift the trophy in nine month's time

View 5 Images Arsenal are the reigning Premier League champions (Image: Getty)

The waiting is finally over. As the Premier League returns tomorrow, the footballing world beckons forth another nine-month rollercoaster of drama and unrelenting tension.

‌



Before a single ball is kicked on opening weekend, the traditional ritual of pre-season predictions has reached fever pitch, with top pundits across the UK weighing in on who will lift the trophy come May.

‌



After weeks of blockbuster transfers and managerial shuffles, opinion among the game's elite analysts remains fiercely split. Will defending champions Arsenal build on their success and forge a new dynasty, or can a refreshed Manchester City reclaim their crown?

‌



Meanwhile, heavyweights like Liverpool, Manchester United and an ambitious, revamped Chelsea are waiting in the wings, eager to crash the party and disrupt the title narrative. Mirror Football looks at who 11 of the UK's leading pundits think will end the 2026/27 season as champions.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

BBC reveals new Match of the Day line-up with six stars missing and four replacements named READ MORE :

Wayne Rooney - Arsenal

Manchester United legend and BBC pundit Rooney reckons Arsenal will be even better than they were in their title-winning campaign after bringing in Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa. He said on Stick to United: "You’re looking at Arsenal and Man City [for the title].

‌



View 5 Images BBC star Rooney has a clear verdict (Image: Stick to United)

"Chelsea will be a lot better this season, Tottenham will be better. You've got Liverpool in there as well. So it’s going to be tough. Arsenal have the potential to run away with it but behind them we could see a lot of changes.

"I think Arsenal are the favourites to win it but can United nick second off Man City and start to build again and maybe challenge for the title next season?"

‌



Joe Hart - Man City

Hart, ex-City goalkeeper and Rooney's BBC colleague, disagrees and thinks his former side have the edge. He said: "It's really important how Arsenal handle the scrutiny of being champions, but they will totally understand that and what is coming their way.

"City were clunky against Arsenal in Cardiff but I don't think they will overreact to one poor game. I think they still believe they've got the team and the quality to challenge," he added, predicting City to finish first and Arsenal to end up second.

Gabby Agbonlahor - Arsenal

"I'm going with Arsenal," the former Aston Villa forward said on talkSPORT. "They've got the strongest squad, they've been there and done it. We can't judge the teams chasing them yet as they've got new managers – Enzo Maresca in at Manchester City, Andoni Iraola at Liverpool, Xabi Alonso at Chelsea."

‌



View 5 Images Agbonlahor is backing Arsenal (Image: talkSPORT)

Danny Murphy - Arsenal

"Without all the new signings being done yet, it's hard to call, but I think Arsenal will win it again," the BBC's Murphy said. "Mikel Arteta's side will have greater strength in depth than last season and more quality. They also have the confidence and belief from winning it last year.

"They have not lost any of their best players and they have got a group who know what the manager expects from them and are completely on board with it. Arteta didn't need to spend half the pre-season drilling them with his methods like a new manager has to."

‌



Jeff Stelling - Arsenal

"I've done my finishing order for the Premier League, so here we go: Arsenal to win it," Stelling began on talkSPORT. "Chelsea second, Man City third, Man United fourth, Spurs fifth, Liverpool sixth... that's my prediction but I'll probably be miles off it."

Jamie Carragher - Man City

At the start of August, Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher tipped Manchester City to win the Premier League title. However, he warned his view would change if they sold Rodri - and that is exactly what has now happened with the Spaniard joining Barcelona.

"I think City," Carragher said on Football Ramble. "The reason I think City is, they were close last year. I know Pep's gone. I get that. But when you've had the same manager for 10 years, the flip side of what people will say - that's it hard to [follow in his footsteps] - but [Maresca] will offer something a little bit new, a little bit fresh.

‌



View 5 Images Carragher is on City's side (Image: Football Ramble)

"I think if Rodri left for Real Madrid I wouldn't be saying that. But I think where they are right now, I'd go with City... I just think City with a new manager will be so invested in the Premier League.

"With Arsenal I do feel like they will be [focused on] the Champions League. Winning the Champions League for Arsenal is far bigger... if you got to March, April and you were still in the Champions League, that's where you'd go, 'Declan Rice, you're not playing Saturday, you're playing Tuesday in the Champions league.' I'm not sure City will have that."

‌



Shay Given - Man City

"I don't think Pep leaving City means we will see what happened when Sir Alex Ferguson left United. Instead, I am expecting the opposite, because of a fresh voice in the dressing room," the former City goalkeeper predicted. "These players have not won the Premier League in two years so they will be hungry for success. City will be number one."

Leon Osman - Arsenal

"Arsenal look like a team that are ready to have a run at winning three titles in the next four or five years," the ex-Everton midfielder said. "Teams like United in the early Premier League days, Arsenal under Arsene Wenger and Jose Mourinho's Chelsea give me the vibes this team does."

View 5 Images Most pundits think the Gunners will go back-to-back (Image: Getty)

‌



Matthew Upson - Arsenal

"Arsenal are my favourites again but I don't see them running away with it," Upson said. "Staying at the top is always harder - ask any manager - and you also have to remember there were spells when they looked like they had run out of steam last season and were grinding out results a lot of the time."

Sam Allardyce - Man City

"I believe Manchester City will win the Premier League," the veteran Premier League boss said on No Tippy Tappy Football. "I think Enzo Maresca will have a great first season, otherwise he'll be out of the door."

Article continues below

Chris Sutton - Arsenal

"Arsenal look like they are at a different level, squad-wise," Sutton told the BBC. "They won the title in a bit of a different way so it will be interesting to see how they go about it this time, but it does look on the face of it like they can beat you up, or just play through you."

As for City, Sutton suggested there were too many question marks hanging over them to pick them as champions. He said: "There's no doubt the pressure will be on Maresca from the off, and replacing Rodri is nigh on impossible. They are in for Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi, who is a talented player but he is 18, and would be a massive gamble."

Sports.title: Six FPL changes you need to know before playing this season
Sports.content:
Six FPL changes you need to know before playing this season

If you're playing Fantasy Premier League this season - here are six changes to the game that you need to know about

View 3 Images Fantasy Football players have just a few hours to lock in their teams (Image: Fantasy Premier League)

With the new Premier League season kicking off tonight, millions of Fantasy Premier League (FPL) managers are frantically tinkering with their squads ahead of this evening's deadline. The annual scramble to build the perfect 15-man team is well and truly underway as we hurtle towards the start of the 2026/27 campaign.

‌



But before you finally click confirm and lock in your squad, there's some crucial housekeeping you need to be aware of. FPL bosses are constantly looking for ways to keep the game fresh and exciting - and this coming year is certainly no exception.

‌



A raft of major tweaks and system updates have been rolled out for the 2026/27 season that could fundamentally alter your strategy - and the makeup of your squad. To ensure you don't get left behind by your rivals, here are six of the biggest changes you need to be aware of.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Nine FPL budget enablers to afford both Erling Haaland and Bruno Fernandes READ MORE :

FPL tips: The five biggest mistakes to avoid in Gameweek 1 READ MORE :

Live updates to your mini-leagues

No longer will you be forced to wait until the final match of the day for your league tables to be updated. This is because FPL has finally introduced real-time updates directly into the game.

You'll now be able to watch your overall rank and mini-league position shift instantly as the goals go in. To add to the drama, projected bonus points will now be added to a player's score after just 20 minutes of each match.

‌



Bonus Points System (BPS) changes

The Bonus Points System has been tweaked this season to give a little more love to attackers, goalkeepers and full-backs. Following the introduction of defensive contribution (DC) points last season, the game-makers want to limit the crossover of players scooping up both DC points and bonus points in the same game.

Players will no longer be punished for being tackled, something which did count towards bonus points last season. The number of clearances, blocks and interceptions (CBIs) needed to earn a BPS point - used to calculate bonus points - has also increased from two to three. That is meant to make it less likely for defenders to score high amounts of defensive contribution points and bonus points.

View 3 Images Erling Haaland was the highest-scoring FPL player last season (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



The way goalkeeper saves contribute to BPS has also been tweaked. Under the old system, a save was worth three points if the shot came from inside the box and two if it was taken from outside. Going forward, every save will be worth two BPS points, regardless of where the shot originated, with the outside-the-box distinction scrapped.

Elsewhere, the number of BPS points for saving a penalty has dropped from eight to seven. However, goalkeepers will also earn an additional BPS point when denying a 'big chance' where the player shooting is expected to score.

Price-change predictions

Trying to predict when a player is going to rise or drop in value has always felt like a dark art. Not anymore. The official game will now feature a progress bar, giving managers a massive hint as to whether a player is about to jump up or down in price.

‌



This new tool will use official FPL data to track the transfer activity for every player, providing the best possible indication of who is likely to rise and fall each day.

Position changes

View 3 Images 11 players have had their FPL positions changed (Image: Fantasy Premier League )

A total of 11 players have had their FPL positions reclassified ahead of the 2026/27 campaign. Four players who were defenders last season have been moved into midfield: Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Lamare Bogarde (Aston Villa), Keane Lewis-Potter (Brentford) and Patrick Dorgu (Manchester United).

‌



Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi is the only player switching from forward to midfielder, while four midfielders have been reclassified as defenders: Mats Wieffer (Brighton), Rio Cardines (Crystal Palace), Ryan Sessegnon (Fulham) and Eric Moreira (Nottingham Forest).

At the other end of the pitch, Manchester City's Omar Marmoush and Brighton's Georginio Rutter have both been moved from midfield into the forward category.

History checker and Gameweek recaps

FPL has introduced a revamped history checker, allowing managers to compare their previous season rankings with those of other FPL players more easily. The tool will also show your rank as a percentage, so you can track your best-ever finish relative to the rest of the game rather than simply looking at your overall position.

‌



There is also a new visual Gameweek recap. Once each Gameweek has finished, managers will be able to view an image summarising their performance, including details of their top-scoring player.

Points locked in later

If you've ever celebrated a dubious FPL assist only for it to be heartbreakingly wiped out hours later, this one is for you. Gameweek points will now be officially finalised at a set time of 9am UK time the morning after the final match of the round.

This extra buffer allows FPL to iron out any late data corrections from Opta, meaning fewer controversial overnight point swings.

Liverpool's Premier League curtain-raiser against Newcastle United is just around the corner. But Andoni Iraola's squad have only welcomed three new additions so far this summer.

In his first season in charge, new manager Iraola, who has supplanted Arne Slot, will travel to St. James' Park on Sunday. But clubs have until September 1 to conclude their transfer business.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey.
