World.title: Las mafias cobran 9.000 euros a los migrantes de la entrada masiva en Ceuta por llevarlos en lancha a la Península
World.content:
Trayectos de horas en pequeñas embarcaciones, por la noche, hacinados y sin chalecos salvavidas ni medidas de seguridad. Un viaje penoso y peligroso, pero también muy caro para ir desde Ceuta hasta la península. Las mafias de trata de personas han encontrado en la entrada masiva de miles de migrantes en Ceuta del pasado 30 y 31 de julio un filón para incrementar su ya lucrativo negocio. La Policía Nacional ha detenido en los últimos días a cinco presuntos integrantes de dos grupos criminales que cobraban hasta 9.000 euros a aquellas personas en situación irregular que quieren cruzar de modo clandestino el Estrecho de Gibraltar para llegar a las costas andaluzas, según ha informado este viernes el Ministerio del Interior. Las últimas estimaciones oficiales cifran en 5.000 los migrantes que permanecen en Ceuta de los más de 80.000 que a finales de julio entraron en la ciudad autónoma. De ellos, más de 2.000 son menores de edad.

En uno de los operativos, los agentes detuvieron a dos personas en Ceuta y otras dos en La Línea de la Concepción (Cádiz), todos ellos varones y de nacionalidad española, según detallan fuentes policiales. Se les imputan delitos de organización criminal y favorecimiento de la inmigración irregular. El quinto arrestado está acusado de participar en el traslado en la noche del pasado 14 de agosto de siete personas en una barca de tan solo cinco metros de eslora y dos de manga que se quedó sin gasolina a mitad de la travesía y llegó a duras penas a una playa cercana a la misma localidad gaditana. El juez ha enviado a prisión provisional a este último por el grave riesgo para la vida que tuvieron las víctimas.

La investigación que permitió la desarticulación de la primera organización se inició tras localizar la policía una embarcación de las conocidas como “lancha rápida o casco”, y que también se usan para el narcotráfico, encallada en un saliente rocoso de la zona costera de Benzú, justo al otro lado de donde se encuentra el espigón de El Tarajal, donde se produjo la entrada masiva de julio. Las pesquisas revelaron que la embarcación, que presentaba marcas y daños característicos de la navegación a alta velocidad, había sido utilizada recientemente para trasladar inmigrantes, aunque los daños producidos al encallar la habían dejado inutilizada.

La Policía constató que la lancha pertenecía a una organización de trata de personas que operaba desde antes de la entrada masiva de julio entre la ciudad autónoma y La Línea de Concepción. La localidad gaditana era, de hecho, su centro de operaciones, desde la que enviaba a Ceuta embarcaciones de pequeño calado para recoger migrantes en situación irregular y llevarlos a la península. Para ello, contaba en la ciudad africana con integrantes que se encargaban de captar a aquellas personas que, procedentes de la entrada masiva, estuvieran dispuestos a pagar importantes cantidades de dinero ―hasta 9.000 euros― por cruzar el estrecho.

Los migrantes que aceptaban eran trasladados a domicilios, garajes y otros lugares de la organización a la espera de que un integrante de la red los trasladase en vehículos al lugar costero donde iban a ser embarcados. En estos desplazamientos, la trama tomaba medidas de seguridad, como evitar las zonas de vigilancia policial, muy reforzada en las últimas semanas por la crisis migratoria. Una vez llegaba la embarcación que había salido de la costa gaditana, los migrantes subían a bordo y se les trasladaba inmediatamente a la Península, donde a las víctimas les estaban esperando otros miembros de la organización para su posterior dispersión en tierra. Para conducir las lanchas rápidas, la trama contrataba pilotos especializados “en navegación rápida” y con experiencia en “realizar maniobras evasivas y sortear los controles policiales”, según destaca la Policía Nacional en su nota. Por este papel cobraban “elevadas” cantidades de dinero.

La segunda investigación se inició el pasado 14 de agosto, cuando a las 4.00 de la madrugada llegó a la playa de El Burgo, cercana a La Línea de la Concepción, una pequeña barca en la que viajaban hacinadas siete personas. Según relataron a los agentes, habían iniciado el viaje antes de la medianoche y habían permanecido cerca de cinco horas en un mar cubierto por una intensa niebla, con un intenso frío y con la ropas empapadas por el oleaje que entraba en la barca. La travesía se hizo aún más penosa al quedarse a la deriva tras agotar el combustible. No llevaban a bordo chalecos salvavidas pese a que casi ninguno sabía nadar. Por todo ello, el único detenido está acusado de un delito contra los derechos de los ciudadanos extranjeros agravado por el ánimo de lucro, la situación de especial vulnerabilidad de las víctimas y el peligro para la vida de estas.

World.title: El Santander gira hacia la banca tradicional en EE UU y añade 60.000 millones en depósitos con Webster
World.content:
El Santander cerró este jueves la compra de Webster, la tercera mayor adquisición de su historia, después de las de ABN Amro y Abbey National, y que supone un giro histórico de la estrategia desplegada por la entidad en Estados Unidos. Suma más de 3,5 millones de clientes adicionales y, sobre todo, gana peso en banca tradicional, tanto de empresas como a pie de calle. Con más de 70.000 millones de dólares (unos 60.000 millones de euros) adicionales en depósitos, sienta las bases para impulsar sus negocios en el país con una estructura clásica: banca de inversión, crédito al consumo, banca minorista y banca privada. El mercado estadounidense se convierte en el tercero más importante por activos para la entidad, por detrás de España y Reino Unido.

Para la hoja de ruta a largo plazo del Santander, Webster es la clave de bóveda, con un peso muy superior al que tiene respecto al balance total del grupo del 4%. El banco adquirido es una plataforma para consolidar su crecimiento en la mayor economía del mundo, que complementa sus negocios en el resto de América y también en Europa, y responde al reiterado mantra de Ana Botín, que desde el inicio de su presidencia ha marcado el valor diferencial del banco con sede en Cantabria en su dimensión internacional.

La operación se cerró este jueves, una vez obtenidos los permisos pertinentes, el último, el de la Reserva Federal, el 5 de agosto. La entidad española ha quemado etapas para ejecutar una compra que estaba pactada con la firma estadounidense desde febrero.El Santander ha abonado por Webster unos 12.500 millones de dólares (10.800 millones de euros), pagados en parte en efectivo y en parte en acciones. El Santander tendrá ocho millones de clientes en Estados Unidos y un balance de 327.000 millones de dólares (unos 283.000 millones de euros). Se convierte en la decimonovena entidad del país, doce puestos por encima de donde estaba, y en líder del mercado en el estado de Connecticut, donde tiene su sede Webster y acapara el 24% de los depósitos. Aspira a obtener ahorros de costes de 800 millones de dólares (unos 700 millones de euros), con un incremento del beneficio por acción del 8% en tres años.

Emilio Botín desembarcó en Estados Unidos hace dos décadas con la entrada en el capital de Sovereign y la compra del embrión del actual Santander Consumer USA. El primero, del que compró el 100% años después, le proporcionó una licencia bancaria y una red en parte del país, mientras que el segundo se convirtió en una máquina de crédito al consumo centrada en facilitar préstamos para la adquisición de automóviles. Este supone el grueso de su negocio en Estados Unidos, que hasta el momento se situaba como tercer mercado del grupo, con el 13,5% de sus beneficios en el primer semestre.

La contrapartida es que, hasta ahora, el Santander en Estados Unidos estaba centrado en créditos al consumo para clientes de segmentos de renta bajos, un sector de préstamos de elevados intereses, pero también expuesto a litigiosidad y alta morosidad. Más de la mitad de su cartera de financiación en el país se destinaba a financiar automóviles. El coste de financiación de estos préstamos era, también, alto, pues el banco no captaba suficientes depósitos: cubría la brecha con emisiones de deuda, por las que abona cerca de un 6%, más que duplicando lo que paga por el ahorro a sus clientes.

Desde esta semana, el Santander es una entidad de perfil clásico, con una amplia base de clientes, una red de 200 oficinas a pie de calle, implantación local y un fuerte peso del crédito a empresas. Webster no tiene ni un solo dólar expuesto a la financiación de vehículos y su cartera crediticia está formada en un 80% por préstamos a compañías, sobre un total de créditos de 58.000 millones de dólares (unos 50.000 millones de euros), según los datos comunicados al supervisor estadounidense de los mercados, la SEC. El dato de provisiones para insolvencias resume la gran transformación: en Webster, suponía el 1,25% de su cartera de préstamos, mientras que en Santander Estados Unidos era del 7%.

Webster complementa este asentado negocio del Santander con una inyección de liquidez cimentada en buena parte en el ahorro de los ciudadanos estadounidenses destinado a cubrir sus gastos sanitarios. Lo hace a través de HSA Bank, especializado en estas cuentas con ventajas fiscales y con una remuneración casi nula. Estas cuentas suman unos 8.000 millones de euros con un interés pagado de apenas el 0,17%, a las que se suman otros 8.600 millones de euros en cuentas a la vista.

Santander también cuenta con un creciente negocio de banca de inversión (CIB, por sus siglas en inglés) en Estados Unidos. Ha fichado a más de 300 personas en unos dos años y ha propulsado este negocio en todos los ámbitos, con unos resultados incuestionables. El importe de las comisiones obtenidas allí en la última década se dispara casi un 800%, hasta los 414 millones de dólares (381 millones de euros) en 2025, de acuerdo con los datos de Dealogic. Webster será el trampolín para elevar el nivel de esta línea de negocio.

Su objetivo es consolidar una franquicia de banca corporativa y de inversión de escala global, reforzando especialmente las actividades de advisory (asesoramiento), financiación, mercados de capitales y soluciones transaccionales. Webster le abre puertas del noreste del país, desde el área metropolitana de Nueva York hasta Rhode Island y Massachusetts. Así dispondrá de acceso directo a uno de los mayores ecosistemas de potenciales clientes de servicios de banca de inversión, con firmas de private equity (capital privado) o especializadas en deuda. La entidad señala en su informe del primer semestre que Webster “representa una oportunidad adicional para ampliar la base de clientes en el país, y aprovechar los beneficios de una mayor escala mediante la colaboración y el uso de la plataforma de Santander en Estados Unidos”.

Lo mismo ocurre con la banca privada, que por primera vez ha superado los 320.000 clientes. La división que engloba este negocio, junto al de gestión de activos y al de seguros, exhibe un RoTE del 57% a cierre de junio. Esa rentabilidad casi cuadruplica la media del grupo (15,6%) y triplica la de la banca corporativa y de inversión (CIB), la segunda mejor área con un 20,3%. Su oficina en Miami, centrada en clientes latinos, será el núcleo que surtirá de clientela a la entidad en Estados Unidos, ya con la licencia para operar en banca privada en todo el país de la mano de Webster. El primer objetivo será retener a los actuales clientes latinoamericanos. El segundo, llegar a los clientes hispanos en Estados Unidos con mayor patrimonio, que en conjunto suman alrededor de un billón de dólares disponibles para invertir.

La marca Webster, por el momento, se mantendrá, como aclara la entidad en su página web y ya adelantó Ana Botín en febrero. Esta marca convivirá con la de Openbank y la propia del Santander. Aunque la marca perviva, el banco estadounidense ha dejado de negociarse en la Bolsa de Nueva York. Sus propietarios son ahora accionistas del Santander, tras haber recibido 2,0548 títulos en forma de ADS (american depositary share) que pueden canjear sin ningún coste por acciones cotizadas en Madrid.

World.title: El Ministerio de Igualdad pide a la Fiscalía que valore estudiar el asesinato de un joven gay en Alicante como delito de odio
World.content:
Fue después de una noche de fiesta, el pasado jueves sobre las 5.20 de la madrugada. En la parada del TRAM del Campo de Golf, en el área de la playa de San Juan de Alicante, dos hombres, Miguel de 27 años y otro de 22, discuten mientras esperan el tranvía que les devuelva a casa. En el transcurso de la pelea, Miguel sufre un traumatismo craneoencefálico que le llevará al Hospital Doctor Balmis de Alicante, donde finalmente fallecerá. Días después, la asociación Alicante Entiende pide que el caso se investigue como agresión homófoba, ya que la víctima era gay. Este miércoles, el Ministerio de Igualdad ha pedido a la Fiscalía que valore como delito de odio la muerte de Miguel, ya que les “preocupa el hecho de que esta agresión pueda tener una posible motivación homófoba”, que constituiría una agravante específica del Código Penal.

A la parada del tranvía metropolitano de Alicante, situada en las inmediaciones de una zona de ocio muy frecuentada, especialmente en verano, acudieron tanto los servicios sanitarios como agentes de la Policía Nacional, que se hicieron cargo de la investigación y arrestaron al presunto agresor. Según publicó el diario local Información, en un primer momento, el arrestado declaró que el enfrentamiento se produjo porque rechazó mantener un encuentro íntimo con la víctima. Por este motivo, la asociación Alicante Entiende solicitó que la investigación contemplara la hipótesis de que pudiera tratarse de un homicidio con motivación homófoba.

Esta solicitud activó el oficio enviado por Igualdad a la Fiscalía, en el que se recoge que el artículo 22 del Código penal regula “las circunstancias que agravan la responsabilidad criminal”, y Julio Valle, el director General para la Igualdad Real y Efectiva de las personas LGTBI+, que es quien firma el oficio, señala directamente al punto cuatro, que fija que es agravante “cometer el delito por motivos racistas, antisemitas, antigitanos u otra clase de discriminación referente a la ideología, religión o creencias de la víctima, la etnia, raza o nación a la que pertenezca, su sexo, edad, orientación o identidad sexual o de género, razones de género, de aporofobia o de exclusión social, la enfermedad que padezca o su discapacidad”.

El Centro de Información y Coordinación de Urgencias (CICU) de la Comunidad Valenciana recibe el aviso de la pelea a las 5.37 horas del jueves. Una unidad del SAMU y otra de Soporte vital Básico (SVB) se desplazan hasta el lugar de los hechos. “Durante la asistencia”, relatan fuentes del CICU, Miguel “entra en parada cardiorrespiratoria”. Los efectivos del SAMU le practican “maniobras de reanimación cardiopulmonar” y logran recuperarlo momentáneamente. Sin embargo, una vez hospitaizado, muere horas después. Cuando el agresor pasa a disposición del juzgado de instrucción número seis de Alicante, en funciones de guardia, ya se ha pasado de una posible agresión a un posible homicidio.

Según explican fuentes del Tribunal Superior de Justicia (TSJ), el sábado 15 por la tarde, tras tomar declaración al arrestado, el juez dicta su “libertad con medidas cautelares de retirada de pasaporte, prohibición de salida del territorio nacional y comparecencia periódica ante el juzgado”. El magistrado considera que “no concurren los requisitos para adoptar una medida cautelar más gravosa, como la prisión provisional”, ya que no aprecia riesgo de fuga porque el interrogado tiene arraigo en el territorio. El detenido “queda investigado en una causa abierta por un delito de homicidio”. De momento, sin agravante por posible delito de odio. Fuentes cercanas a la investigación consultadas por EL PAÍS señalan que tampoco la Policía Nacional aprecia indicios de homofobia.

Inicialmente, Alicante Entiende, asociación que defiende los derechos de la comunidad LGTBI, emite un comunicado en el que transmite su preocupación ante la posibilidad de que “la orientación sexual de la víctima y las circunstancias de la agresión no reciban la consideración que merecen”. Solicita que “los delitos de odio por orientación sexual sean investigados y juzgados con todas las garantías, que se esclarezcan las verdaderas motivaciones del crimen y que la homofobia no quede invisibilizada ni normalizada”. Su dirección convoca una concentración frente a las puertas de los juzgados de Benalúa para reivindicar su posición.

Sin embargo, poco después, el abogado del presunto agresor, José Manuel Yepes, niega en otro comunicado la agresión homófoba, ya que “no se corresponde ni con la realidad de lo sucedido, ni con lo que consta en las actuaciones, ni con la propia resolución judicial, que refleja una dinámica de los hechos sustancialmente distinta de la que se está difundiendo públicamente”, asegura. En el mismo documento, el letrado afirma que su defendido “pertenece al colectivo LGTBI, ha sufrido desde su infancia y juventud rechazo y bullying precisamente por su orientación sexual y participa de la lucha contra cualquier forma de homofobia”. Estas declaraciones frenan las iniciativas de Alicante Entiende, cuyo coordinador, José Ramón Samper, declara a EL PAÍS que han desconvocado la concentración y tratan de “conformar y contrastar, de manera oficial, que el presunto agresor sea homosexual”.

Sí sigue en pie, adelanta, un encuentro organizado por familiares y amigos de Miguel, en su memoria, en la Plaza del Ayuntamiento de Alicante, el jueves a las 20 horas.

En el escrito de Igualdad, el ministerio refleja también las repercusiones políticas que ha levantado el caso. Compromís ha pedido “transparencia, celeridad y claridad” en la investigación de los hechos y considera “imprescindible” que permita “determinar con rigor qué pasó y si detrás de la agresión hay un delito de odio LGTBIQfóbico”. El diputado autonómico Francesc Roig, también portavoz de Igualdad LGTBI de la formación nacionalista, reclama que se frenen las “especulaciones” con una investigación “clara, justa y honesta” porque “cualquier otra cosa implicará una falta de respeto a la memoria de la víctima y de todas las víctimas de los delitos de odio”. Roig solicita que la Generalitat se persone en este caso porque ante la gravedad de los hechos “no puede mirar hacia otro lado” y que utilice “todos los instrumentos jurídicos e institucionales a su alcance para defender los derechos de la víctima y contribuir al esclarecimiento de los hechos”.

Por su parte, Sumar País Valencià ha registrado cartas dirigidas al presidente de la Generalitat, Juanfran Pérez Llorca, a la vicepresidenta primera y consellera de Igualdad, Susana Camarero, al alcalde de Alicante, Luis Barcala, y a la concejala de Bienestar Social, Begoña León, para reclamar una “respuesta institucional conjunta”. Uno de los coordinadores de Moviment Sumar País Valencià, Xavier López, apunta en un comunicado que no se puede esperar a saber si se trata de un crimen homófobo “para defender políticas que prevengan la LGTBIfobia”. “En estos momentos corresponde a la investigación policial y judicial determinar qué pasó y cuál fue la motivación de la agresión. No podemos prejuzgar los hechos y mucho menos atribuir una responsabilidad penal que corresponde a los tribunales. Pero respetar la investigación no significa mirar hacia otro lado”, ha advertido López, que pide que todas las hipótesis se investiguen “con rigor” y sin descartar ninguna prematuramente.

El consistorio alicantino, liderado por el Partido Popular con apoyos puntuales de Vox, prefiere mantenerse cauto. El vicealcalde de Alicante, Manuel Villar (PP), ha afirmado que se trata de un hecho “dolorosísimo”, pero que, mientras no sepan el origen o la causa, no van a hacer declaraciones sin “ningún tipo de base”. “Es arriesgado hacer afirmaciones cuando se está en fase de investigación”, concluye.

World.title: Adiós lavanda, hola girasoles: un viaje por Burgos cuando en agosto cambia de color
World.content:
Cuando los tonos morados desaparecen de los campos, el amarillo toma el relevo en la comarca de La Bureba o la Ribera del Duero, con Briviesca, Poza de la Sal y Caleruega como paradas principales para descubrir el patrimonio burgalés

En agosto, Burgos cambia el perfume por la luz. Al recorrer los campos de la provincia por carreteras secundarias y caminos, el viajero aprecia una muda de color: la lavanda que en julio pinta hectáreas de morado deja paso a los girasoles, que colorean de amarillo vastas extensiones de La Bureba y algunos paisajes de la Ribera del Duero.

Quien quiera rodearse de miles de girasoles —esas flores que Van Gogh volvió universales— debe acudir durante esta época del año a La Bureba. Allí los girasoles aparecen a los lados de las carreteras, y se convierten en uno de los grandes protagonistas del paisaje durante unas semanas. Caminar junto a los campos en su momento más vigoroso puede justificar por sí solo la visita a esta comarca y sus pueblos.

Más información Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj

El mejor punto de partida para entender el paisaje estival de esta comarca burgalesa, que, además, fue de las primeras en adquirir personalidad dentro del condado castellano, es la localidad de Briviesca. En esta época del año los girasoles se muestran en su máximo esplendor y embellecen aún más al pueblo. Briviesca invita a detenerse y mirar los campos más allá de su condición de cultivo. La iniciativa Girasoles con Arte, puesta en marcha en 2024, combina el patrimonio urbano de Briviesca y el paisaje agrícola mediante dos trazados sencillos: uno de 1,63 kilómetros y otro de 2,67 kilómetros.

La plaza Mayor de Briviesca, en la provincia de Burgos. Teo Moreno Moreno (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Quienes deseen conocer más a fondo el ambiente local en torno a los girasoles pueden combinar paseos junto a ese paisaje efímero con una visita más detenida por el pueblo. La propuesta puede realizarse en medio día, y se puede iniciar con una etapa más urbana. Esta se desarrolla a lo largo de distintos puntos de interés de la localidad conocida como La Bien Trazada, por su plano ortogonal con forma de tablero de ajedrez. Comienza en la plaza Mayor, el punto desde el que la localidad muestra su trazado rectilíneo. En el centro se levanta un templete musical de estilo modernista construido en 1909. La siguiente parada está a escasos metros, en la excolegiata de Santa María la Mayor, iniciada en el siglo XIV y reformada en el siglo XVIII. La ruta continúa hacia el monasterio de Santa Clara, cuyo interior alberga un retablo de más de 20 metros de altura, tallado en madera de nogal y singular por carecer de policromía. La ausencia de color permite apreciar la minuciosidad de la talla, que bajo una capa de policromía podría haberse relegado a un segundo plano. Esa falta de acabado, atribuida a problemas económicos, terminó por convertirse en una de sus particularidades más reconocibles.

Retablo mayor en la nave central de la Iglesia de Santa Clara. Miguel Sotomayor (GETTY IMAGES)

Pero el encanto del girasol en La Bureba no se queda solo en Briviesca. El viaje continúa hacia Poza de la Sal, un recorrido que lleva al viajero a través de extensas hectáreas doradas cercanas a los pueblos de Quintanabureba y Llano de Bureba. En Poza de la Sal, el amarillo del verano encuentra un contrapunto mineral e histórico: una villa encaramada al borde de la llanura, con el castillo de los Rojas en lo alto y las antiguas salinas hundidas en el diapiro que dio nombre al pueblo. Conocida también como el Balcón de la Bureba, permite una vista amplia sobre la llanura de la comarca antes de volver a la carretera.

Un campo de girasoles cerca de Poza de la Sal. Architect´s Eye / Alamy / Cordon PRess

Al sur de la provincia, el amarillo cambia de compañía. Mientras que en La Bureba crece junto a cereales y llanuras, en la Ribera florece entre viñas y el recuerdo reciente de la lavanda. Después de la siega, la lavanda permanece en aceites esenciales, aguas florales, jabones, perfumes y otros productos elaborados en la zona. Así, Caleruega y Cilleruelo de Arriba han empezado a construir en el sur burgalés una pequeña cultura alrededor de esta planta.

Una calle en la localidad burgalesa de Poza de la Sal. Jose Luis Alvarez Esteban (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien se acerque a Caleruega para seguir el rastro dorado en los terrenos que circundan al pueblo entrará también en un lugar que no se entiende sin su más ilustre personaje: Santo Domingo de Guzmán, patrón provincial. Al llegar al casco urbano, el Torreón de los Guzmanes se yergue con 17 metros de altura desde época medieval sobre el resto de la arquitectura local. Le acompaña el Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, fundado en 1266 por mandato del rey Alfonso X el Sabio, que en su interior alberga un claustro gótico y el Pocito de Santo Domingo, donde la tradición sitúa el nacimiento del santo y al que se atribuyen propiedades milagrosas. En lo alto del casco urbano, la iglesia de San Sebastián, de piedra románica, vigila la plaza mayor del pueblo desde el siglo XII. De esta parroquia procede la pila donde fue bautizado Santo Domingo, trasladada fuera de Caleruega y utilizada en bautizos de miembros de la Casa Real española desde 1605.

El claustro del Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, en la localidad de Caleruega. Blanca Saenz de Castillo (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien quiera detenerse más tiempo en la zona encontrará, además de los campos de girasoles que acompañan algunas carreteras de acceso, otros puntos de interés. El Sendero de las Loberas, de 10,2 kilómetros, permite acercarse a esas construcciones circulares de piedra que servían para resguardar el ganado de los lobos. En el entorno de Caleruega también aparecen otros vestigios, como los yacimientos arqueológicos de San Mamés y La Pudia o la Bodega de Alfonso VIII, vinculada al despoblado de San Martín de Bañuelos.

La ruta en busca de más hectáreas doradas por el sur de Burgos puede prolongarse por la Ribera hacia el pueblo vecino de Baños de Valdearados. Allí, la Villa Romana de Santa Cruz recuerda la huella de Roma en el territorio, mientras que a finales de agosto la fiesta en honor a Baco, dios romano del vino, llena el pueblo de togas, desfiles, mercado y vino de la Ribera (este año se celebra el 22 y 23 de agosto).

Celebración de la Fiesta a Baco, en Baños de Valdearados. Carlos Mora (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Otra parada cercana es Villanueva de Gumiel, que permite prolongar esa continuación amarilla del verano por los campos de la Ribera. En sus calles se aprecian las fachadas de las casas antiguas, con una arquitectura caracterizada por plantas bajas de mampostería de piedra y plantas altas de entramado de madera y adobe. La iglesia de San Mamés, del siglo XVII, se diferencia de otras formas tradicionales al estructurarse en dos naves simétricas con ocho arcos cruzados y un valioso retablo del siglo XVI.

Recorrer con calma estos pueblos burgaleses permite disfrutar de un manto dorado que parece no agotarse desde la carretera. En estas tierras, la floración suele regalar sus mejores imágenes entre finales de julio y agosto. Y a quienes busquen mejores fotos suele convenirles acercarse al amanecer, momento en el que los rayos de sol iluminan de frente las cabezas maduras que miran hacia el este.

Como en toda floración agrícola, el estado de cada parcela cambia según la siembra, el calor y el momento de cosecha, por lo que conviene consultar con las oficinas de turismo antes de emprender la ruta. Y, sobre todo, conviene recordar algo crucial: estos campos no existen para la foto, son cultivos en activo. Hay que respetar todas las flores para que el siguiente visitante pueda admirar los campos de esta Castilla con la misma belleza.

World.title: Government condemns Israeli West Bank settlement plan
World.content:
The Netherlands has joined six other governments in condemning Israel’s decision to open bidding on a major settlement project in the occupied West Bank, and called on the Netanyahu regime to withdraw the plans immediately.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and the leaders of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Norway called the project “unacceptable” in a joint statement, and said they have “grave concerns” over the potential impact it could have on achieving peace in the region, particularly amid “unprecedented levels of violence by settlers against civilians.”

Israel’s construction and housing ministry opened bidding on Tuesday for 1,234 homes, part of a wider plan for 3,401 settler homes in E1, an area east of Jerusalem. Contractors have until October 19 to bid, a week before Israeli elections.

Critics say the project would split the West Bank in two and cut East Jerusalem off from it, making a contiguous Palestinian state impossible.

The condemnation comes as the Netherlands prepares to enforce its own ban on settlement goods, which takes effect on September 22. The three-year measure bars the import, sale and trade of goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories.

The Netherlands is also the main EU entry point for produce grown in Israeli settlements, according to research published in June, handling around a third of such shipments reaching the bloc.

Settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law. The E1 plan, approved last year, faces a legal challenge in Israel, where a court has asked the state to respond to the petitions by September 1.

Police in Sittard in Limburg shot a man outside the city’s police station on Stationsplein overnight Friday due to what they called a “suspicious situation”.

The suspect, a 34-year-old man from Nijmegen, was injured in the leg and received first aid on the scene. He was then arrested and transferred to hospital.

Police shootings are rare in the Netherlands. Last year, officers shot at people 15 times.

Still, the national police are investigating the incident, as all cases involving an officer shooting that results in injury or death must be looked into.

Police are also looking into the cause and background of the incident.

World.title: New medicine gives hope to Dutch narcolepsy sufferers
World.content:
Some 8,000 Dutch people suffer from narcolepsy, a sleep disorder that leaves sufferers spontaneously falling asleep during the day.

Now, for the first time, a new drug approved earlier this month in the US is being touted as the first to target the disease’s roots rather than its symptoms.

“I have been trying to give people a reasonable life for 40 years,” Gert Jan Lammers, special professor of sleep disorders at Leiden University Medical Centre, told broadcaster NOS. “With this medicine, we finally saw real improvement.”

Several of his patients participated in the drug’s research trials, and he says the results are positive. “People feel normal again. I’ve been working on this for 40 years now and I haven’t seen this before. It doesn’t work perfectly for everyone, and it doesn’t work all day, but it’s fundamentally different from what we’ve been able to do so far.”

The drug, Orzeyful (oveporexton) still has to be approved by the European Medicines Agency before being prescribed in the Netherlands, which will likely not happen until at least the end of next year.

But for those who have taken it, including Dutch trial participants who can continue using it before its approval here, it’s been a life-changer.

“It’s like you’re finally getting a good pair of glasses,” says Leontien Sickenga, who has taken the drug for one and one-half years. “With other medication I saw the world a bit better, but with this medication the world is clear. When I’m awake, I’m really there.”

In addition to falling asleep in the day, Sickenga also suffered from muscle relaxation and sleep paralysis, common in narcolepsy patients. “It’s very drastic,” she said.

How it works

According to the US Food and Drug Administration, narcolepsy “is caused by the loss of brain cells that produce orexin, a chemical messenger that regulates wakefulness, sleep, and muscle tone.”

Without orexin, the brain has trouble controlling the boundaries between sleep and waking, resulting in narcolepsy’s debilitating symptoms. But the new drug, rather than trying to relieve those symptoms, “directly activates the same brain receptor that the body’s own orexin would normally stimulate, restoring the missing signal.”

Professor of sleep diagnostics Sebastiaan Overeem, who was not involved in the drug’s research, is positive. “This is fundamentally new and very promising,” he says. “Of course, there are no miracle cures, and we still have to see how this drug works in the long run. But in the field, everyone is impressed.”

Side effects of the drug include urinating more, and it’s not yet known how effective it will be in the long-term.

“I don’t want to be too positive, because some things we can’t know yet” says Lammers. “But so far, all the signals are on green.”

World.title: Frisian asylum center to remain open, frustrating locals
World.content:
The ministry of justice and security informed the municipality of De Fryske Marren earlier this week that the asylum seekers’ centre in Balk, which was due to permanently shut its doors on October 1 2026, will remain open for another three years, upsetting local officials.

“For the municipal executive, the following applies: a deal is a deal,” says the municipality’s website. “The fact that the agreements cannot be fulfilled now causes disappointment and frustration.”

And, reports Omrop Fryslân, will lead to legal action.

The asylum centre opened in 2016 for what was supposed to be five years. That period was extended several times, most recently in 2024, when a deal was also made to reduce the number of refugees living in the centre from 500 to 225.

While the number of asylum seekers has been reduced, refugee settlement agency COA said the lack of alternative shelters means it can’t meet the October closure deadline.

Closure not an option

“We have been looking for other solutions for as long as possible”, said COA’s Joeri Kapteijns. “However, we have the legal and social responsibility to welcome and guide people safely and with dignity. As a result, closure without an alternative is not an option.”

Closing the Balk shelter, said COA, would “mean that 300 people, families and children, will be on the streets.”

The municipality says it doesn’t want to see people on the streets, but it’s unacceptable that the deal has been broken.

“Although De Fryske Marren wants to prevent residents from being left without suitable shelter from a human point of view, it does not accept this situation,” said the municipality. “The responsibility for the residents and replacement shelter lies primarily with COA.”

But COA says the nationwide shortage of asylum spots means it takes time. “Although fewer people are registering for asylum in the Netherlands than before, the number of residents at our locations is increasing.” Some 80,000 people currently live in asylum centres.

COA attributes the problem to long asylum procedures and too few homes for people with a residence permit, meaning more people have to stay longer in shelters. “There are fewer new locations opening than there are closing,” it said.

The 300 asylum seekers in Balk, however, fulfil De Fryske Marren’s shelter obligations under the country’s distribution laws.

World.title: Ajax win at Sion, Twente lose at home in Conference League
World.content:
Ajax and FC Twente played the first legs of their Conference League play-off ties on Thursday evening, the last stage before the competition’s league phase. Ajax won 4-2 away at FC Sion in Switzerland, while Twente lost 1-0 at home to FK Qarabag.

Ajax fell behind to a goal just after 30 minutes but recovered after the break. Julian Brandt and Marcos Leonardo scored to put the visitors in front, before Sion equalised from the penalty spot through Ylyas Chouaref.

Tolu Arokodare headed in within a minute of coming on to restore the lead, and Davy Klaassen lobbed a fourth late on.

The match was shown in the Netherlands only on a €4.99 pay-per-view channel, a decision that had angered many fans in the build-up. Ajax will go through as long as they avoid losing by three or more goals in next Thursday’s return at the Johan Cruijff Arena.

Twente jeered at home

Twente had a good start in Enschede but faded, and Kady Borges scored shortly after half-time to hand Qarabag the lead. The home crowd began jeering the team, whistling at the players at full time and cheering the substitution of striker Wout Weghorst.

Qarabag, multiple-time Azerbaijani champions, reached the Champions League knockout stage last season. Both Dutch clubs had come through the previous qualifying round last week. Twente now face a difficult second leg in Baku next Thursday.

World.title: Earthquake of 2.8 shakes northern Groningen
World.content:
An earthquake measuring 2.8 on the Richter scale struck the north of Groningen in the early hours of Friday, the heaviest to hit the region since March.

The epicentre was near the village of Zandeweer, in the Het Hogeland area, at a depth of three kilometres, the meteorological agency KNMI said. The quake was recorded at around 5.50am local time.

Residents in the nearby villages of Uithuizen, Kantens, Rottum and Middelstum said they had felt the tremor, broadcaster NOS reported. No damage or injuries had been reported by Friday morning.

The KNMI classed the quake as an “induced earthquake”, meaning it was caused by gas extraction. Tremors linked to drilling tend to occur closer to the surface, making them easier to feel; those measuring 1.5 and above are noticeable.

Extraction from the main Groningen field stopped two years ago, but the KNMI has warned that quakes can continue for decades as the ground settles. Gas is still being pumped from smaller fields in the province, where drilling is permitted until the end of 2032.

The last comparable tremor was a 3.0 quake near Eleveld in Drenthe in March. The strongest of the 31 induced quakes recorded near the Groningen field last year was a 3.4 tremor at Zeerijp in November, among the heaviest ever measured in the province.

World.title: Bruls calls on justice ministry to enforce motorway tractor ban
World.content:
Local politicians have called for nationwide rules to be enforced to keep tractors off motorways in the wake of a fatal crash during a farmers’ protest a week ago.

Hubert Bruls, mayor of Nijmegen and chair of the board of regional safety councils, said it was “incomprehensible” that local authorities took different approaches to enforcing the traffic rules.

Last Friday two people died in a collision on the A59 at the tail end of a queue that had built up on the A59 near Hees, a suburb of Nijmegen.

Police and the prosecution service had said before the collision happened that they would not prosecute farmers who drove tractors onto the motorway, even though they are prohibited, citing the right to demonstrate.

The prosecution service has since said that anyone who drives a tractor onto the motorway will be subject to enforcement, even though police said at an earlier demonstration that they did not have enough evidence to go on because the farmers had taped over their numberplates.

Bruls told NOS he wanted to hold talks with the justice ministry to decide on a national strategy for offences on the motorway.

“It’s not manageable for the police if every mayor comes up with their own guidelines and the rules change every 10 or 15 kilometres. Some things should be agreed at a regional level.

“For motorways we need to have a national approach because the motorway network covers the whole country.”

Prime minister Rob Jetten said following last week’s deadly crash it was “unacceptable” for farm vehicles to be on motorways. “It leads to very dangerous situations,” he said.

World.title: Max Verstappen signs Red Bull extension on eve of Dutch GP
World.content:
Four-time Formula One world champion Max Verstappen has signed an extended contract with Red Bull Racing, ending speculation that he could leave the team or quit the sport altogether.

Verstappen, 28, was rumoured to be contemplating a move to rivals McLaren or Mercedes in recent months, but in a press release on Thursday he said he had chosen to stay with the team he saw as a “second family”.

”We have the best people and I’m excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again,” he said. “This remains the ultimate goal that all of us have been working towards and will continue to pursue.”

He dismissed reports he had been in talks behind the scenes about a possible move to McLaren next season. “I was closer to quitting than changing teams,” he said.

The news that Verstappen will keep driving for Red Bull until 2030 will be welcomed by Dutch fans on the eve of the last edition of his home Grand Prix this weekend.

“To make this announcement during the last Grand Prix at Zandvoort is a great moment for me as well,” Verstappen said. “Hopefully we can give the fans a special send-off for the final race.”

Hybrid cars

Verstappen won the first three races after Zandvoort returned to the Formula One calendar in 2021, at a time when he dominated the sport, winning 71 races in 10 years and four consecutive world titles between 2021 and 2024.

This year he is standing sixth in the championship race, 110 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli, and is yet to record a win.

Verstappen has criticised the new hybrid cars introduced this season, that require drivers to save on fuel by recharging the battery during the race, describing them as “not fun to drive” and “anti-racing”.

Earlier this season he took part in the 24-hour race at the Nürburgring in Germany. Verstappen said being able to drive more endurance races in future years was “one of the factors and wishes” that influenced his decision to sign a new deal.

He was also caught up in the tensions within the Red Bull team surrounding the departure of former team boss Christian Horner, who left just over a year ago after being accused of sexually harassing a female colleague.

Horner was twice cleared of wrongdoing, but left with a £52 mln (€60 mln) payout amid accusations by Verstappen’s father, Jos, that he was “driving people apart”. Horner later said Max Verstappen played no role in his departure.

World.title: New official tasked with promoting Poland criticised over error-strewn, potentially AI-generated report
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. A government official appointed last month to promote Poland abroad has been hit by a wave of criticism after it emerged that she authored a report containing errors and which shows signs of being generated by artificial intelligence. The document mislocated major Polish cities and included bizarre language mixing Polish and English. It was marked as being part of a project financed by the sport and tourism ministry, though the ministry itself has denied that claim. The opposition has called on prosecutors to investigate potential misuse of public funds. ⁉️ Czy “Markę Polska” ma nam wygenerować sztuczna inteligencja? ⁉️ Czy Ministerstwo Sportu i Turystyki zapłaciło 200 000 złotych w ramach zadania publicznego za raport wygenerowany przez AI? ⁉️ Czy mogę prosić Panią Minister prof. @b_mroz_gorgon o odniesienie się do tych pytań… pic.twitter.com/lM2AY88oAh — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 The official in question, Barbara Mróz-Gorgoń, is a professor at Wrocław University of Economics who was appointed three weeks ago as the government’s plenipotentiary for the promotion of Poland’s brand, a newly created position. She was presented at a press conference by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. However, this week, journalists and commentators began highlighting cases of bizarre errors from a report, titled A Self-Portrait of the Poles (Polaków Portret Własny), published last year with Mróz-Gorgoń named as the author, in her position as president of a think tank called Marka Polska (Brand Poland). The report contained some glaring errors, such as describing the city of Katowice as being in “north central” Poland (whereas in fact it is in the south) and Wrocław as being in the “northwest” (when it is actually in the southwest). Geografia – czyli gdzie leżą Katowice A propos miast jest też ciekawy chochlik lub też, jakby to powiedział ktoś złośliwy, klasyczna halucynacja AI. Przy opisie badań FGI miasta opisane są w następujący sposób (zdjęcie poniżej): 👉 Olsztyn – północny wschód 👉 Szczecin -… pic.twitter.com/SF6XBRfhWS — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 Other parts contain strange analysis, such as noting that “after World War Two, Germany did not build its brand on the Holocaust”. The text also features unusual language, including random use of words in English, some of which have been turned into Polish ones. It is also regularly features words written in capital letters. One sentence, for example, refers to “INSTABILNOŚĆ” and “REZILIENCE”, presumably meaning “instability” and “resilience”, but neither of which is a Polish word. Another section claims that 95% of Poles born after 1990 are “polilingwalni” (an invented Polonised version of “polylingual”) who speak “angielski fluent”, a strange linguistic mix that means they speak English fluently. As well as the unusual language, the very claim that 95% of young Poles speak fluent English, as well as that many additionally speak Mandarin, has been questioned by many commentators. The report also contains bizarre errors in footnotes, which are numbered randomly (on one page, three consecutive footnotes are numbered “41, 517, 6”) and some of which are completely empty. A number of expert commentators have suggested that the text contains clear indications that it was generated by AI, a claim supported by evidence from programmes that check texts for AI-generated content. AI czy nie AI, oto jest pytanie Czytając ten raport kilkukrotnie, trudno mi było pozbyć się wrażenia, że nikt poważny, a szczególnie naukowiec z tytułem doktora habilitowanego, nie wygenerowałby dużych części raportu, za który zapłacili podatnicy, w jakimś LLM. No bo przecież… pic.twitter.com/jyTexgmeXS — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 As well as bearing Mróz-Gorgoń’s name as author, the report also features on its front cover the logo of the sport and tourism ministry. The first page then includes a note saying that the project was carried out under an initiative co-financed by the ministry. After the issue began to draw attention and criticism on Thursday, the ministry issued a statement saying that the report was not ordered by them, was not part of any agreement to which the ministry was a party, and that no request to use the ministry’s logo was submitted. However, a social media post last November by deputy sport and tourism minister Piotr Borys shows him attending an event to present the report. He thanked Mróz-Gorgoń for coordinating the project and inviting him to the presentation. 📚W Akademii Leona Koźmińskiego odbyła się prezentacja raportu „Polaków Portret Własny”, przygotowanego Think Tank Marka Polska. To wyjątkowe wydarzenie poświęcone premierze badań dotyczących DNA Marki Polska. 🧬To pierwsze tak kompleksowe badanie, które pokazuje, kim jesteśmy… pic.twitter.com/jb7KdCJTPM — Piotr Borys (@piotr_borys) November 26, 2025 On Thursday evening, Mróz-Gorgoń herself addressed the controversy in an interview with Polsat News. She said that the report was actually a “work in progress” that “should never have appeared in the public space”. However, she still defended the work, saying that “the research was conducted reliably” and “the conclusions stand up to scrutiny”. But she also admitted that the writing of the report had been “aided by artificial intelligence”. In separate remarks to the Polish Press Agency (PAP), she said that “we used AI tools solely for transcription, summarising and text editing; they did not design research content or draw conclusions…We worked according to social science methodology, diligently and without cutting corners”. Meanwhile, on the Marka Polska think tank’s website, where the report had been published, it was initially changed on Thursday to being marked as a “draft version” before later being deleted entirely. Od raportu i deklaracji, że “praca badawcza [została] przeprowadzona zgodnie z zasadami nauk społecznych, rzetelnie i merytorycznie, w oparciu o opisaną metodologię”, przez “work in progress”, aż do “Oops! That page can’t be found”. Myślę, że to słowo “Oops!” jest najlepszym… pic.twitter.com/OaSTxkwKwa — Sebastian Meitz (@MeitzPL) August 20, 2026 On Thursday evening, the main opposition party, Law and Justice (PiS), announced that it was submitting requests to both prosecutors and the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (ABW) to investigate the use of around 200,000 zloty (€46,380) in state funds for the project that the report was allegedly part of. PiS has also called on Mróz-Gorgoń to resign or to be fired. On Friday, a deputy digital affairs minister, Dariusz Standerski, told the Wirtualna Polska news website that “all the circumstances surrounding the creation of this report will be clarified”. The controversy around Mróz-Gorgoń comes just days after the sport and tourism ministry was involved in the launch of a new advertising campaign designed to encourage tourism to Poland, but which many commentators have argued was poorly conceived and executed. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to attract tourists from Europe and the US. The first video, under the slogan "Poland. A speed of 253 km/h (157 mph) has been reached by a Pendolino train during tests carried out as part of preparations to speed up rail connections between Poland’s major cities from next year. The plans will see the journey time between Warsaw and Kraków cut to well under two hours. “Polish rail is accelerating – and 250 km/h is just the beginning,” declared the infrastructure minister Dariusz Klimczak, alluding to plans for Poland to later begin running trains at speeds of up to 320 km/h. Osiągnęliśmy 250 km/h na Centralnej Magistrali Kolejowej❗🚅 Dzisiejsze nocne testy systemu GSM-R na linii nr 4 zakończyły się pełnym sukcesem. Oznacza to, że pociągi pojadą tą trasą z rozkładową prędkością 250 km/h już w przyszłym roku❗ Pozwoli to znacznie skrócić czas… pic.twitter.com/ndXvePZP4t — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) August 18, 2026 The tests on the GSM-R data transmission system, a communication standard designed to be used at very high speeds, were carried out on Monday night. Trains will be able to run on Poland’s Central Main Line (CMK), which connects Warsaw with Kraków and Katowice, at a scheduled speed of 250 km/h from December 2027. That will cut the expected journey time between Warsaw and Kraków, the country’s two largest cities, by around half an hour to 1 hour and 52 minutes, reports rail news service Portal Kolejowy. It will also be possible to travel from the capital to Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, in around three hours. The fastest current connection is 3 hours and 30 minutes. Reaching the target speed of 250 km/h was a “very important moment for Polish rail”, said Maciej Kaczorek, a board member of PKP Polskie Linie Kolejowe, the state railway infrastructure manager, quoted by news website Money.pl. Poland has been operating Pendolinos, built by France’s Alstom, since 2014. The trains are designed to run at speeds of up to 250 km/h, but currently operate at a maximum of 200 km/h in Poland and run on routes connecting Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław and the Tricity area. However, this week’s tests are not a record rail speed in Poland. In 2013, a Pendolino reached 293 km/h during a test on the CMK a year before the high-speed trains commenced passenger services in the country. A Polish Pendolino high-speed train has begun running in the Czech Republic for the first time. The Prague-Bohumín service will run until June as part of a certification process that Polish operator PKP Intercity hopes will lead to a Warsaw-Prague route https://t.co/hmUNd7ft0E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 10, 2026 Speaking to Rynek Kolejowy, deputy infrastructure minister Piotr Malepszak said that it had “taken too long” for the network to be adapted to allow regular speeds of 250 km/h. The current government, which took power in December 2023, has much broader plans for expanding high-speed rail travel in Poland, including building 2,700 km of tracks capable of carrying trains at 320 km/h. In December 2025, state rail operator PKP Intercity launched a tender for 20 such trains. They would cut the journey time between Warsaw and Gdańsk, on Poland’s Baltic coast, to around 100 minutes – from 2 hours 25 minutes currently – by 2040, Malepszak told the Polish Press Agency in June. Passenger numbers on Poland’s rail network have been booming in recent years. In the first half of 2026, a record 44.7 million passengers travelled with PKP Intercity, more than 10% up on the previous year’s record and some 45% higher than three years earlier. Poland has launched a tender to buy 20 trains that can reach speeds of 320 km/h (199 mph), making them the fastest ever to travel on Polish tracks. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has unveiled plans to reduce income tax rates for an estimated 3.5 million people earning around or slightly above average salaries. The costs of the cuts would be covered by increasing the tax rate for large companies and individuals with the highest earnings. The changes, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk says are intended to “provide relief and assistance to the growing middle class”, would come into effect from next year – when the government is facing re-election. However, the proposals still require approval from parliament, where Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, has a majority, and President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of bills. 📊 Nowa skala PIT będzie lepiej dopasowana do rosnących wynagrodzeń. Do 130 tys. zł pozostaje stawka 12%, między 130 a 150 tys. zł pojawi się 24%, a 32% zacznie obowiązywać dopiero powyżej 150 tys. zł. 💰 #WięcejWPortfelu pic.twitter.com/1S2MpSkVoC — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 19, 2026 The main elements of the proposed changes, which were outlined by Tusk and finance minister Andrzej Domański on Wednesday, are an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €27,800) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. Tusk noted that, since his government took office, wages in Poland have increased by around 30%, bringing increasing numbers of people into the higher tax bracket. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, in June this year, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,401.58 zloty, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. “We’re not talking about millionaires here; we’re talking about a growing middle class…on whose shoulders the financing of state security, defence spending, etc. rests to a large extent,” said Domański. “We want to change this…so that those who work hard to earn their average wage can clearly feel the relief,” added Tusk. “And we want this to be financed by the wealthiest companies and the wealthiest individuals, who have the lowest tax burden.” The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Therefore, in order to finance the middle-class tax cuts, Tusk and Domański announced that the government would seek to increase corporate income tax from 19% to 22% for firms and tax capital groups that generate annual revenues above €50 million. Meanwhile, the solidarity levy for individuals earning over 1 million zloty a year would be increased by one percentage point, to 5%. “I am absolutely convinced that this will make our tax system more equitable,” declared Tusk. However, he also conceded that raising the income-tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 zloty – as his Civic Platform (KO) party promised to do within its first 100 days in office – would not be possible for budgetary reasons, in particular the need to finance high defence spending. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) tax free. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build savings and channel money into the domestic financial market https://t.co/1xDHHJGYKX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 14, 2026 The prime minister said that the planned tax changes would be discussed further this week at a cabinet meeting devoted to next year’s state budget, which is currently being prepared. The relevant legislation will subsequently be submitted to parliament, with the aim of bringing it into force in 2027. However, Tusk acknowledged that there is a strong possibility of a veto by Nawrocki, who has blocked dozens of government bills, including fiscal measures. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increase in the tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. Last month, he effectively blocked a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits by sending it to the constitutional court for review. However, he did approve a law increasing the corporate income tax rate for banks. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Next year’s budget will be closely watched given that Poland’s fiscal situation has become increasingly problematic in recent years. In 2024, the European Union placed Poland under its excessive deficit procedure, requiring Warsaw to commit to measures to bring down the deficit. However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record. The situation has led two of the big three rating agencies, Fitch and Moody’s, to shift Poland’s credit outlook to negative. This year, Fitch warned that the political gridlock between Nawrocki and the government was making tackling the deficit and debt more difficult. Given that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in autumn 2027, it is unlikely that either the government or Nawrocki – who will be supporting the right-wing opposition – will be keen on any fiscal measures that either raise taxes or reduce spending in areas such as social policy and defence. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. The country is already under the EU's excessive deficit procedure, requiring it to take steps to bring public finances under greater control https://t.co/LNJ0YrP2Ge — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland launches tourism campaign featuring Lewandowski, Eisenberg and Rubik
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to promote itself internationally and attract more tourists from “key European markets” and the United States. The new initiative, which has the slogan “Poland. More than you expected”, features global Polish icons such as football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, and Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, who received Polish citizenship last year. A series of videos, the first of which was released Tuesday, will aim to present Poland as “modern, safe, diverse and authentic”, as well as “defying stereotypes”, says sports and tourism minister Jakub Rutnicki. Commissioned by his ministry and launched by the Polish Tourism Organisation (POT), the campaign will be conducted in Germany, Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States. The first video promotes Warsaw, Poland’s capital, and features Lewandowski, Rubik and Eisenberg appearing near the city’s landmarks. Polish actor Nikodem Rozbicki, meanwhile, plays the role of renowned 19th-century Polish composer Fryderyk Chopin. In the 30-second spot, Chopin’s character declares that Warsaw is “where my heart is” – a reference to the fact that Chopin’s heart, preserved in cognac, was brought back to the city from Paris by his sister shortly after his death in 1849 and is now immured in a pillar in the city’s Holy Cross Church. Lewandowski, who recently joined US football team Chicago Fire, tells viewers that Poland offers “more than you expected”, a reference to the campaign’s main slogan, which suggests to viewers that Poland may surprise them positively. “Research shows that people who have visited Poland rate it much more favourably than their previous perceptions or media reports suggested,” notes POT in its press release. Magdalena Krucz, the head of POT, adds that she believes the campaign “will be as surprising to audiences as Poland itself is to tourists who come to us for the first time”. However, the slogan is not new: it has been used by POT to promote Poland since 2021. The new campaign will also feature Nobel Peace Prize winner and former president Lech Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that brought down Poland’s former communist regime. POT notes that he remains “one of the most recognisable symbols in the world of the fight for freedom and democracy”. The music is arranged by Radzimir Dębski, better known as Jimek, a Polish composer and conductor who has regularly performed with US rap legend Snoop Dogg. Polish-American NBA star @JeremySochan has joined a campaign to promote Poland as a tourist destination. His appearance has been received positively, but Sochan responded directly to one commentator who said a black person shouldn't be advertising Poland https://t.co/KXDok7IAXP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2024 Poland has experienced a tourism boom in recent years. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation, behind only Malta. The biggest tourist draw is the historic city of Kraków, which was last year named the best city break destination in Europe by members of British consumer association and magazine Which? for the fifth time. This year, Time Out magazine rated Kraków the 16th best city in the world. However, the country has a wide range of tourist-friendly destinations, including long, sandy beaches on the northern Baltic coast, mountains in the south, the lake district of Masuria, as well as many historic cities and modern museums and galleries. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 The city of Lublin in eastern Poland, which will be a European City of Culture in 2029, last year welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors, including over half a million from abroad. The city is known for its rich Jewish history, and featured prominently in the 2024 Oscar-nominated film A Real Pain, directed by and starring Eisenberg, whose ancestors were Jews from Lublin and the nearby town of Krasnystaw. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP within a decade, from about 5% now. The strategy includes creating a “Polish brand” through which internationally recognised athletes, artists, historical figures and products are showcased more prominently. Last month, the government appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. The city of Lublin in eastern Poland welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors in 2025. That included 506,000 from abroad, which was also the highest ever figure, with Brits, Israelis and Americans the most common foreign visitors https://t.co/6yMrRcf6ml — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 28, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she visited parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is PiS’s main opponent. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland “99% sure” fugitive opposition politician is in pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that they are “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia. Last week, judicial authorities in Poland confirmed that they had received a letter purportedly from Romanowski, who is wanted in Poland for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. In the document, Romanowski claimed to be in Transnistria and requested safe passage back to Poland. However, as the authenticity of the letter had not been confirmed, some media outlets speculated that the politician may not, in fact, be in Transnistria. Meanwhile, the Moldovan authorities quickly announced that they had no record of Romanowski travelling to Transnistria, which is a landlocked territory that only has borders with Moldova and Ukraine and operates no commercial passenger flights. A former government minister who fled criminal charges in Poland appears to be in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. Marcin Romanowski's whereabouts have been unknown since he left Hungary earlier this year https://t.co/MPWroFVbMe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Speaking on Tuesday morning, Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, said they have “still not confirmed” the veracity of Romanowski’s claim to be in Transnistria, reported broadcaster RMF. However, shortly afterwards, speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said he wanted to address the issue given there has been “a great deal of speculation and misinformation regarding Mr Romanowski and his whereabouts”. “I can say that the intelligence services of other countries in the region with which we cooperate have confirmed to us the information that Mr Romanowski is 99% certain – I say that just in case – to be in Transnistria, in Tiraspol,” he continued, referring to the capital of the breakaway region. "Pan Romanowski znajduje się na 99 procent w Naddniestrzu. Chyba nie trzeba tu komentarzy" Donald Tusk podczas posiedzenia rządu ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/muVQVKrOTs — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 18, 2026 Transnistria is a narrow strip of land in eastern Moldova that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s as the Soviet Union collapsed, fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Its flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. Various experts and former intelligence officials have noted that it would be impossible for Romanowski to enter without Russia’s approval. The fact that Romanowski appears to be hiding there has led to criticism of PiS, the party Romanowski still technically serves as an MP and which publicly takes a strongly anti-Russian position. “If it is true that [Romanowski] is in Transnistria, a republic not recognised by anyone, de facto controlled 100% by Russia, then it must have happened through and with the participation of Russia,” said defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz last week. “Escaping under the Russian umbrella is the worst possible thing, because not only are they cowardly, but they are also joining the enemy of Poland,” he added. In his remarks today, Tusk said that Romanowski’s likely presence in Transnistria “speaks for itself regarding not only Mr Romanowski but the entire political group that covered up for and benefited from such people, and continues to cover up for them”. PiS politicians have largely avoided commenting, noting that it has not been confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. However, deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek last week admitted that, if Romanowski did trael there, he would have “crossed a line”. Nie wyprzedzajmy faktów – powiedział poseł PiS Zbigniew Kuźmiuk, pytany, czy Marcin Romanowski może zostać zawieszony w partii.https://t.co/IQzuS8Ad7O — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 14, 2026 Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government from 2019 until 2023, when the party lost power to a new ruling coalition led by Tusk. In 2024, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 11 crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group and using crime as a source of income. However, he instead fled to Hungary, where he was granted asylum by the then-government of Viktor Orbán, a PiS ally. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, his successor, Péter Magyar, promised to extradite both Romanowski and Zbigniew Ziobro, the former PiS justice minister who had also fled criminal charges in Poland and been granted asylum by Orbán. However, as Magyar was sworn in as the new prime minister, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains, and Romanowski disappeared, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians deny the accusations against them and claim to be victims of political persecution by Tusk’s government. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In his comments on Tuesday morning, Nowak said that prosecutors had found “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. Polish prosecutors are still, however, attempting to confirm Romanowski’s whereabouts and secure his extradition to Poland to face justice. He is subject to a European Arrest Warrant. However, that applies only in EU countries, and Moldova is not a member of the bloc.
